preloadSoundIds.doc: eight SNDS resource ids in the code segment that sound_preload_fixed copies to the stack and cache_preloads at startup. The address comes from the mov esi, 0x32448 at 0x32543. By SNDTABLE (listing/resource_tables.txt) they are 189 MECBBAAT, 247 MECTURX2, 219 MECGCLX1, 240 MECSEXX1, 246 MECTRDXX, 207 MECBYHLX, 206 MECBSYRX and 254 MECXLOCK. What each sound is for is not established here. Labelled as its first dword; the other seven follow at stride 4

object_cull_main_view.doc: The MAIN 3D view's object cull, installed as objectCullHook by the frame render in vfx_video, the default that pass restores after its special passes. Read from the disassembly (0x3f500..0x3f779), because the pointer-reached body has no C of its own. If the flag at 0x96ef4 is set, an object whose type family (bits 4-7 of +2) is 0xa0 returns 1 at once. Then, with (dx, dy, dz) = object position - view translation and r the radius: if dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 > (farClip + r)^2, with farClip read from +0xb4 of the viewer at 0x9701c, it returns 5 (beyond the far clip, as a sphere test, not a plane). Otherwise it computes the view depth from Viewer.rotation row 2 (cullDepthRow, 0x14fe7c...) and stores it in objectViewDepth at 0x3f60f, the value render_object_list uses for LOD and depth sorting. The lateral tests that follow, and the return codes of the paths after 0x3f62a, were not read. It is a LABEL, not a named function: the Ghidra project has no function here, because it is reached only through code that stores it in objectCullHook, which the data-pointer sweep does not see.

crash_divide_overflow.doc: where a divide error resumes, via crash_stub_divide: 'Divide Overflow - exiting'. Read from the disassembly, because it is reached only through a rewritten exception frame and has no function of its own in the project. It increments crashDepth and switches on the old value through a four-entry jump table, so each re-entry skips one more step. At depth 0 it runs vfx_video_sub_010780 (which frees the render scratch pool, among other things not read here), game_boot_sub_0158e0 and input_sub_048c20. It then sprintfs and log_writes the short message, runs main_sub_049f40, and prints the long 'MechWarrior II ...' message through clib_sub_06261a. At depths 1, 2 and 3 it enters one step later each time. At depth 4 and beyond it goes straight to clib_sub_062096(1), the exit path every depth ends in.

At depths 1, 2 and 3 it enters one step later each time. At depth 4 and beyond it goes straight to clib_sub_062096(1), the exit path every depth ends in.

crash_stub_divide.doc: DPMI exception-0 handler installed by install_crash_handlers: reloads DS from crashHandlerDS, points the exception frame's EIP:CS at crash_divide_overflow and far-returns

crash_stub_gpf.doc: the same stub shape pointing at crash_general_protection. Not installed by install_crash_handlers, and no reference to its address was found in the image

crash_stub_page_fault.doc: DPMI exception-0xe handler installed by install_crash_handlers: reloads DS, points the frame's EIP:CS at crash_page_fault and far-returns

equipmentRatingBuckets.doc: 23 rows of three shorts {slotCodeFloor, value, count} in the CODE segment, copied to the stack by mech_loadout_rating (mov esi, 0x4c6d0 at 0x4cf40) and used as buckets. A slot code falls in the highest row whose floor is below it and increments that row's count, and each row then adds count * value * tons, or count * -value flat when value is negative. Floors and values: 5000 1, 5050 1, 5100 -60, 5150 -60, 5200 -50, 5250..5650 1, 5700 2, 5750 0, 5800 (gyro) 2, 5850 (engine) 3, 5900 (life support) 2, 6000 (heat sink) 1, 7000 (jump jet) 1, 8000 0, 9000 0. Codes over 9000, the ammo bins, land in the last row and add nothing. A non-zero count in the 8000 row doubles the slot-count term. The count column starts at 0 and is live data, not configuration

mtblMarkName.doc: the string '$'. project_chunk_exec's MTBL branch, after mission_table_load, calls mission_mark_by_name with it and makes it the name later chunks in the stream attach targets under (0x4eb01, 0x4eb06 - the only two references). So objectives named '$' would collect the targets of whichever stream loaded their table. None of the 2059 objectives in MW2.PRJ is named '$', so in the shipped data this path marks nothing and, for the rest of that stream, attaches nothing

mainViewWindow.doc: the viewportModes window the main view is drawn in when non-zero: vfx_video_sub_010490 memsets the buffer at 0xa46fc and viewport_select()s it at the start of a frame. 0 in the data. Its ONLY writer is an unrecovered routine at 0x106a0 that stores its argument clamped to 0..10 (anything outside -> 0), and nothing calls that routine or points at it - so in the shipped game this stays 0 and the letterboxed windows 1..3 are never used

lightObjectFollow.doc: while set (and 0x954fc, set alongside it), vfx_video moves lightPos to lightObjectRecord's position every frame before drawing. Set by the LITO chunk (lightobj) when its object resolves; effect_spawn clears it while an explosion is the light and sim_slots_update sets it again. Only 2 of the scene files, CIN2PLT1 and TEALPLT1, carry a LITO chunk

lightObjectRecord.doc: the world record whose position the light follows - LITO chunk +8, a project id put through project_mangle_id and world_record_find; -1 for none

backdropNode.doc: SceneNode of the FIRST world-chain object whose type family (type & 0xf0) is 0x90, found by vfx_video_sub_0103c0 (called from main), which also moves its subtree to the aux list with scene_subtree_move_to_aux_list. The CONSUMER is the main view render in vfx_video_sub_010490: before anything else in the scene it sets the far clip to 0x7fffffff, swaps objectCullHook to its own routine (0x3f780), draws this tree with render_scene_tree_sorted, then restores the far clip and object_cull_main_view. Drawn first and never far-clipped: a backdrop behind the world. Family 0x90 is six meshes in MW2.PRJ (TL1MARDM, TL1TANA, TL1PDSTL, TL1SIDWK); what they depict was not established.

cockpitHeadNode.doc: SceneNode of the FIRST world-chain object whose type family is 0xa0 - the mech HEADS (KF5_HEAD, BM5_HEAD ...) - found by vfx_video_sub_0103c0. The CONSUMER is vfx_video_sub_010490: only while cockpitViewActive, and AFTER render_object_list has drawn the world, it sets the near clip to 8, swaps objectCullHook to its own routine (0x3f970), draws this tree with render_scene_tree_sorted and restores both. So in the cockpit view a head model is drawn over the scene - the cockpit shell. It is simply the first head on the world chain; that this is always the player's own mech was NOT traced.

frameProjCount.doc: records in frameProjTable. Starts at -1, which frame_prj_add takes as 'not yet cleared' and answers by clearing all 96 slots first

anim2dCount.doc: slots handed out by anim2d_add, starting at 0. Only anim2d_add touches it (every fixup to it is in that function) and nothing decrements or resets it, so anim2d_free does NOT make a slot reusable: at most 7 ANM2 chunks are ever accepted per run of MW2.EXE

messagePanes.doc: the two message slots' panes (ViewWindow x 2): {&defaultCanvas, 0, 0, 1.0, 1.0} as 16.16 fractions in the image; message_bar_layout lays them out

messageSlots.doc: the two message-bar slots (MessageSlot): 0 the top bar, 1 the bottom

mapHeightLow.doc: PLNT chunk [12]; default 0. The bottom of the overhead map's height ramp. vfx_video_sub_0115e0 LOWERS it by 1000 (10 m) each time it sets the map up, then sets mapHeightRange = mapHeightHigh - mapHeightLow. vfx_video_sub_011910 extends the ortho view's far distance by -mapHeightLow when it is negative, so ground below zero stays inside the view. That the decrement repeats on every set-up, rather than once, is what the code says. Whether set-up happens more than once per mission was not checked. IN MW2.PRJ 41 of the 46 PLNT chunks give high 3500..50000 with low 0. The other five give HIGH 0 and LOW 10000 (three) or 40000 (two), so mapHeightRange is negative and the ramp runs backwards - lower ground maps to the upper shades. Whether that is deliberate (inverted shading) or a swapped pair in the data is not established; a port should reproduce the arithmetic, not guess

mapHeightHigh.doc: PLNT chunk [11], stored with mapHeightLow when either is non-zero; default 6400 (64 m). The world height at which the overhead map's shading reaches the top of its 16-step ramp: map_height_shade computes (height - mapHeightLow) * 16 / mapHeightRange. vfx_video_sub_0115e0 recomputes mapHeightRange from this when the map is set up

mapHeightRange.doc: mapHeightHigh - mapHeightLow, the divisor in map_height_shade

screenModeSizes.doc: 3 x {width - 1, height - 1}: (319,199), (639,479), (1023,767). Only screen_select_asset_variant reads it, looping 0..2 at stride 8 and comparing [0] with screenModeInfo[0] - 1 and [1] with screenModeInfo[1] - 1; the index of the nearest becomes assetVariant

brightness.doc: the monitor brightness 0..15: main takes it from mw2snd.cfg +0x28, brightness_commit changes it

brightnessShown.doc: the brightness table every palette upload goes through: palette_set_entries maps each entry by brightnessTables[brightnessShown] before the DAC write. brightness_preview sets it, commit and revert set it back to brightness; main starts it at brightness. CORRECTION: the first note called it only the table palette_apply_brightness was last asked for

dayPhasePaletteSlot.doc: int, stride 8, interleaved with dayPhaseFadeTicks: the palette slot each phase fades to - 4, 0, 4, 8 for phases 0..3 (from hour 5, 7, 17, 19). So slot 0 is day, 4 dawn AND dusk, 8 night - the groups PALG fills four at a time. A fifth pair (-1, 360) follows; no index reaches it

dayPhaseFadeTicks.doc: int, stride 8, beside dayPhasePaletteSlot: 2730, 2730, 3640, 2730 ticks - 15, 15, 20 and 15 s at 182 Hz. day_cycle_set_phase overrides it with 0x16c (2 s) for the first fade of a mission, and with 0xb6 (1 s) when leaving the 0xa55e9 overlay mode

dayPhase.doc: the phase day_cycle_set_phase last faded to, 0..3, or -1 for none so the next call always fades

gravity.doc: the planet's gravitational acceleration, loaded per mission - sim_object_dispatch_by_type computes it as a project chunk field times 0x794 >> 0x10 and is the only writer. Everything that falls reads it: the mech movement integration takes -gravity as its vertical acceleration, falling_object_attach seeds a slot with the same, and the cockpit view uses it too. The reading is settled by the jump jets - ai_group_part1 computes (gravity - MechLoadout.jetDeltaY), thrust cancelling weight, and jetDeltaY is already established from the game printing it as jet_ddy. UNITS: 0x794 = 1940 is ONE EARTH GRAVITY in 16.16 centimetres per 182 Hz tick squared - 980.665 cm/s^2 / 182^2 * 65536 = 1940.2 - so the chunk field is the planet's gravity in g, 16.16 (0x10000 = 1 g). THE PLNT RECORD, since this handler reads the whole thing: an 80-byte chunk, dwords indexed with the tag at [0] and the length at [1]. [2] gravity in g; [4] -> 0x957c0, 365 in all 46 records, read only by vfx_font code - RESOLVED, it is daysPerYear; [5] -> 0x957bc, read by the same - RESOLVED, dayLengthSeconds;[9] ambientTemperature, from -200 to 90 in the data; [10] -> 0x961e4 when positive, a divisor in the jump-jet vertical step, meaning not established - RESOLVED, it is jetClimbLimit, the terminal climb speed x 20 in cm/s; [11]/[12] -> 0x955bc/0x955b8 when either is non-zero, read by vfx_video - RESOLVED, mapHeightHigh / mapHeightLow, the elevation range the overhead map shades across; [13] slopeThreshold when positive - 19 of the 46 records set 0x10000, which a 16.16 normal component can never exceed, so on those worlds slope never changes a mech's speed, and 15 leave it 0 for the 0x2000 default; [14] ejectDisabled = ([14] == 0); [15] damageShadeRaises - CORRECTION: this said '-> 0x96ebc, which nothing reads'; polygon_resolve_colour reads it at 0x38e38 (the C and the scan both missed it until that function was recovered), 1 in 16 of the 46 records; [16] effectLightsAllowed (formerly effectCameraCutsAllowed) = ([16] == 0), and 42 of 46 records set it, so effect lighting is rare; [17] and [18] skyEnabled / groundEnabled = (value == 0); [19] -> 0x97044 = ([19] == 0), which render_sky_and_ground reads to allow one extra draw when sky is visible and the horizon sits within 0x97088 of the viewport bottom (the call is clib_core_sub_059e77, taken only while 0x97024 - now shadedFillEnabled - written by HUD widget code, is set); what that draw is, is NOT established - RESOLVED, it is the horizon haze band, and 0x97044 is horizonBandEnabled; see horizonBandHeight. FOR A PORT: [4], [5], [11], [12] and [19] feed only display code (vfx_font, vfx_video, the sky fill), and [15] feeds only polygon shading, so the sim-relevant PLNT fields are [2], [9], [10], [13], [14] and [16]. [3], [6], [7] and [8] are never read - [7] is 0x6978 in 44 records and 0x41eb0 in 2. Counted by walking the BWD resources' chunk streams as the game does (tools/dump_objectives.py's walker): 46 PLNT chunks, gravity 0.6 to 1.3 g. CORRECTION: this note first said 49 records, 20 with slope 0x10000, 17 with 0, 45 without camera cuts, temperatures -80 to 20 and [7] 0x6978 in every record - all from a byte search for 'PLNT' that also counted stale copies in FREE space, the same mistake corrected on missionRecordState. Two of those claims were not just inflated but false. This is one of the two independent constants that fix the world unit as 1 cm; see MechLoadout.speed.

gravitySetting.doc: the mission gravity as the mission record states it, before scaling. vfx_font computes it as (gravity << 16) / 0x794, which exactly inverts the line in sim_objects that produced gravity from record[2] as (record[2] * 0x794) >> 16 - so this holds that record field back again. Two consumers divide by it, so it reads as a divisor rather than an acceleration: falling_object_randomise_motion scales debris launch speed by it, and ai_group_part1 divides a mech field by it. (That mech field is MechLoadout.speed, divided once in mech_std_create: top speed goes as 1 / g. The value is 16.16 g - 0x10000 at 1 g - set by day_cycle_init before any create hook runs.) GHIDRA HAS IT TYPED AS A POINTER, which is why it prints as PTR_LAB_000957b4 and why every use casts it back to int. It is a scalar; the label does not change the type.

climChunkValue.doc: where the CLIM chunk puts the signed short at its +0x0c - and the whole of what MW2.EXE does with CLIM. It is WRITE-ONLY: the store at 0x4e708 in project_chunk_exec is the only relocation that targets it, so nothing reads it. The rest of the 32-byte chunk is not read at all. In MW2.PRJ all 46 CLIM chunks, one per planet beside its PLNT, carry 24 zero bytes after the header. So despite the tag, planetary climate lives in PLNT - ambientTemperature is its [9] - and a port can parse CLIM and drop it. Its source keyword is 'planet', the same as PLNT's (project_tag_to_keyword pairs tag ids 3 and 6 with one keyword), so the two cannot be told apart by keyword alone

dayLengthSeconds.doc: PLNT chunk +0x14 ([5]); default 86400. day_cycle_tick takes the time of day modulo this, and day_cycle_init puts the phase boundaries at /24 * 5, 7, 17, 19. In MW2.PRJ 300 to 50000, most planets 1000 or 6000 - days of minutes, not hours

daysPerYear.doc: PLNT chunk +0x10 ([4]); 365 in all 46 records and in the image. Only day_cycle_tick reads it, as the modulus for dayOfYear

dayOfYear.doc: INIT chunk +0x14 as a signed short; 0 in every INIT in MW2.PRJ. day_cycle_tick advances it mod daysPerYear when the day wraps. No reader of the value was found beyond that increment, so nothing visible depends on it

timeOfDay.doc: seconds into the planet's day. INIT chunk +0x10 sets the mission's start (default 43200, noon); day_cycle_tick rewrites it every 10 s. Not normalised on load: PROVPLT1 starts at -20000, and C's % keeps a negative sum negative, so that mission stays in phase 3 (night) until simTick passes 20000 s

timeOfDayAtStart.doc: timeOfDay latched by day_cycle_init; day_cycle_tick adds simTick/0xb6 to it

ambientTemperature.doc: the planet's temperature, PLNT chunk [9] (-200 to 90 in the data). Its one consumer is mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config), which picks each mech's per-heat-sink dissipation rate from it: COLD is below -30 and HOT above 50. For every mech but the player's, and for the player at difficulty 1, the rate is 100 cold, 50 temperate, 45 hot. At difficulty 0 the player gets 140 cold, else 70. At difficulty 2 the player gets 67, 45 and 36. A difficulty above 2 would give the player a flat 50. Full table and evidence on MechLoadout.heatDissipation. CORRECTION: this said 'below -30 gives full heat dissipation, above 50 cuts it to 45%'. Cold DOUBLES the temperate rate rather than giving some 'full' rate, and hot cuts it by a tenth (50 to 45), not to 45%

ejectDisabled.doc: per-mission, and the whole of the ejection outcome hangs on it. sim_objects sets it from the mission record as (record[0xe] == 0), in a run of six flags all inverted the same way. When it is set, mech_eject refuses: it plays cue 0x20 and leaves status alone instead of writing 5, and the status-5 tick rewrites 5 (ej) to 4 (dd) and sets missionEndCode to 4 rather than 2. ui_callbacks_sub_019da0 deliberately forces it to 0 around an command_execute (formerly option_toggle)(0x3b) call and puts it back afterwards, which is what establishes the direction - that path wants the ejection to go through. ONE READER was unexplained: ai_group_part1 at the 0x170d threshold gates a mech_on_destroyed (formerly ai_log_new_leader) call on this being non-zero. With that function now known to be the mech-destroyed handler, the reading is: when ejection is disabled, the path that would eject the mech destroys it instead. That is consistent with the rest of this note, but the 0x170d site itself has not been re-read.

launchGreyRamp.doc: 16 RGB triples, a grey ramp (0,0,0 206,210,218 ... 7,7,8), 8-bit: boot_load_launch_anims shifts each byte right by 2 in place and writes them to DAC entries 0..15 once the launch picture has faded in

simTick.doc: the '%6ld' timestamp in every AI log line. UNITS: ticks of a 182 Hz timer, so 0xb6 is one second and 0x71c ten. sim_clock_step reads it from stopwatch_elapsed each frame; see that function for the derivation from AIL_set_timer_divisor(timer, 0x199c)

tickDelta.doc: how many 182 Hz sim ticks this frame covers: simTick minus simClockLast, x8 under timeCompression and /4 under timeExpansion (sim_clock_step). Every per-tick rate in the sim is multiplied by it, which is why it appears beside heat dissipation and AI steering. Earlier described only as 'per-tick scale factor', which was the use without the unit

simClockMode.doc: 0 reads simTick from the stopwatch; 3 advances it a fixed 12 ticks per frame instead. sim_clock_step itself enters 3 while the flag at 0x95828 is set - saving the old mode at 0x9584c and pausing the counter with timer_set_paused(0x80, 1) - and on the way out resumes the counter and stopwatch_set's it to the stepped simTick, so real time picks up where the fixed steps left off. Netplay also writes this field directly. NOTHING KNOWN WRITES 0x95828: only sim_clock_step reads it, and no pointer to it exists in the data segment, so what requests the fixed-step mode is not established. Values other than 0 and 3 are not established either

timeCompression.doc: command_execute (formerly option_toggle) command 0x89 flips it and posts 'Time compression enabled/disabled'; sim_clock_step multiplies tickDelta by 8 while it is set. Only honoured when 0x982fc is non-zero

timeExpansion.doc: cheat_handle_command sets it and posts 'Time expansion enabled/disabled'; sim_clock_step shifts tickDelta right by 2 while it is set, so the sim runs at quarter speed

simFrameMinTicks.doc: sim_clock_step busy-waits until simTick - simClockLast reaches this. check_launched_by_shell sets it to 0xb6 / N from a numeric command-line argument (case 4 of its switch), which is a cap of N frames per second - 0xb6 being one second of 182 Hz ticks

simStopwatch.doc: stopwatch slot of the sim clock: sim_clock_step reads simTick from it in its normal mode (simClockMode 0) and writes it back after time compression; sim_stopwatch_elapsed reads it raw

netStopwatch.doc: the second stopwatch slot, read only by netplay: a client adds its elapsed ticks to simTick in a frame that brought nothing from the master, and resets it every exchange

simClockLast.doc: simTick as of the previous sim_clock_step; tickDelta is measured from it

quitRequested.doc: set to 1 by every quit request. The requests are: command_execute (formerly option_toggle)'s command 0x50, any key while exitPromptShown (key_command_update), mission_results_update (formerly exit_prompt) 20 seconds after the player's group's mission result, and main itself when netplay_start (formerly netplay_sub_0446d0) returns 0. main reads it to advance quitCountdown once; netplay_frame_exchange (formerly netplay_opponent_left) returns early while it is set

quitCountdown.doc: main's frame loop runs while this is at most 2. A quit request adds 2 and sets quitRequested; main then adds 1 once, on the first frame that sees quitRequested, latched by a local. Every requester runs before that check in the frame, so from 0 the count is 3 by the end of the frame the request came in and the loop exits at the top of the next: the current frame completes and no further one runs. More requests in the same frame only raise the count and change nothing. main's failed-network start sets it straight to 3, so the loop never runs. Why the count is split into +2 and +1 instead of a flag is not established

missionTaskList.doc: head of the task list main runs every frame with task_list_run, between key_command_update and mech_dispatch_hook1. project_chunk_exec pushes onto it with task_create(&missionTaskList, projectEntryHandlers[i], ...) at 0x4f7e3 when a TSK ('task') chunk runs. main's reference at 0x15d7b is the only other one in the image, so every task on it comes from the mission file. 0 (empty) in the image

simOptions.doc:
pointer to the rule-toggle block (see SimOptions), loaded from mw2dif.cfg by sim_options_load, and what the cheat console writes to. Each byte is 1 when the feature its own message names is on. 
  +0 unlimited ammo   (typed: enolagay)
  +1 invulnerability  (typed: blorb)
  +2 splash damage    (toggled from the targeting UI)
  +3 collision damage (toggled from the targeting UI; was recorded here as 'fall damage' - see SimOptions.collisionDamage)
  +4 heat tracking    (typed: coldmiser)
  +5 difficulty, 0 to 2. mech_config uses it twice: it picks a triple of counts (1,3,4 / 3,3,4 / 4,4,4) and it scales the PLAYER mech heat sink rate together with ambientTemperature - 140 or 70 at level 0, 100 or the default at 1, and 67 / 45 / 36 at level 2 for cold, temperate and hot. Every other mech gets 100 / 50 / 45 for cold / temperate / hot - the same as the player at difficulty 1. CORRECTION: this note said 'Other mechs always get 50', missing that the non-player path at 0x4ce0a still takes the cold and hot branches; see MechLoadout.heatDissipation.
CORRECTION: an earlier pass recorded the polarity as 'NOT uniform', on the grounds that +1 clear enables the MASC malfunction roll while +3 and +4 set enable their features. That was a misreading, not a quirk of the data: +1 is invulnerability, so an invulnerable mech simply does not malfunction. Every byte reads the same way round.

playerMechIndex.doc: compared against a mech's own index

noCrashHandlers.doc: set by the /D command-line switch, which the argument parser in netplay.c reaches as case 2 of its switch on toupper(letter) - 'B', so the letter D. That case also sets hangAround. main skips install_crash_handlers while it is set, leaving faults to the DOS extender, which is what a developer under a debugger would want

keepPlayerControls.doc: set by the -R command-line option. Its one reader, mech_std_create (the test at 0x268fe), skips zeroing ControlState throttle, advance_nav and autopilot when the mech being created is the player's; every other mech has them zeroed

gamePaused.doc: 1 while the game is paused, 0 otherwise. game_update_pause is its only reader and writer: it sets it on the frame ui context 4 becomes active, after freezing the sim clock and pausing sound, and clears it on the frame the context clears, after resuming both

cheatWinMission.doc: set to 1 by the cheat 'icanthackit' (cheat_handle_command, listing/cheats.txt). mission_results_update then gives every undecided table result 2, success, on its next pass, as if all its required objectives had succeeded

currentTask.doc: the task node task_list_run is ticking right now, republished before every callback so a callback can find itself - task_current hands it back and task_data reaches its record. Node layout, all six dwords used by the driver: [0] callback and liveness flag, [1] data, freed on removal, [2] period, [3] last-run tick, [4] next-due tick, [5] next node. task_remove and task_create set it too, so it names the node being created or destroyed as well as the one being ticked. The callback protocol is four messages in the first argument: 0 init from task_create, 1 tick from task_list_run, 2 destroy from task_remove, and -1 rebuilt from task_list_notify_rebuilt, which world_record_replace sends when it rebuilds the tasks' object (this note said three messages until -1's sender was found). Returning 0 from init or from a tick removes the task

menuRepeatStopwatch.doc: -1 in the image; menu_open creates the stopwatch (family 0x100) on first use and resets it; menu_poll_key times the analog axes' repeats with it

menuControlInitFns.doc: control +0x10: init(menu, control), called by menu_item_slider on event 1 before it reads the value. ui_callbacks_sub_0198c0 ([1]) copies menu +5 into the control's selector +0xc, so it can re-aim a control when the menu opens. 3 entries, [0] null. Bounds are the run of code pointers up to the next table, NOT a limit any code checks.

optionAccessors.doc: getter/setter pairs for about 21 settings: entry i queries, entry i+21 writes, and the two are always functions at adjacent addresses. The bodies are one-liners over a global flag word, e.g. get returns (flags & mask) == 0 while set clears the bit when its argument is non-zero - so the setter's parameter reads as 'disabled' rather than 'enabled'. No name table sits beside it, so which index is which option is not established.

menuControlGetFns.doc: control +0x14: get(sel) returns the current value; sel is control +0xc. Pairs by name with menuControlCommitFns where the setting is a plain on/off or level (texture_type_enabled / texture_type_set_enabled, lod_quality_is_high / lod_quality_set, lance_get_formation / lance_set_formation), but the two tables are indexed separately and do not line up past [5]. 17 entries, [0] and [8] null. Bounds are the run of code pointers up to the next table, NOT a limit any code checks.

menuControlPreviewFns.doc: control +0x18: preview(sel, value) - applies a value live without saving it. sound_seq_sub_0437f0 ([1]) sets the playing volume or music state and nothing else, against sound_seq_sub_0439a0 (commit) which also writes the saved-settings block at *0x97e3c. menu_item_slider calls it on each event while its item is selected. 4 entries, [0] and [2] null. Bounds are the run of code pointers up to the next table, NOT a limit any code checks.

menuControlCommitFns.doc: control +0x1c: commit(sel, value) - applies AND saves. sound_seq_sub_0439a0 ([2]) writes both the live value and the saved-settings block at *0x97e3c; texture_type_set_enabled, lod_quality_set, debris_set_enabled and the lance_order_* commands are here too. menu_item_slider calls it on event 4. 21 entries, [0] and [12] null. Bounds are the run of code pointers up to the next table, NOT a limit any code checks.

menuControlRevertFns.doc: control +0x20: revert(sel) - restores the live value from the saved block, undoing preview. sound_seq_sub_043b10 ([1]) copies *0x97e3c's saved value back for each selector. menu_item_slider calls it on event 5. 3 entries, [0] null. Bounds are the run of code pointers up to the next table, NOT a limit any code checks.

menuItemDrawFns.doc: item +5: called for each item as the menu is drawn, as (pane, control, index, item, x, y, menu); [3] is menu_item_slider, [8] lance_slot_target_name. 9 entries, [0] null. Bounds are the run of code pointers up to the next table, NOT a limit any code checks.

lanceTargetNameFn.doc: a pointer to lance_slot_target_name, which lance_status_init stores as the Status line's suffix callback

menuOnLoadFns.doc: menu +0x11: called once by menu_resolve_callbacks after the menu's indices are resolved, as (ctx, menu); bit 0 of the result is ANDed into the load's success. ui_callbacks_sub_0196b0 ([2]) rewrites the menu's own item records, so these customise a menu to the game state. 5 entries, [0] null; [5] onward are small integers (1, 7, 7 ...), not code. The run of code pointers ends there; no code checks an index limit

calibrateDrawToggle.doc: menu_item_calibrate runs its calibration on every other call: it flips this between 0 and 1

lanceOrderSelected.doc: five ints, one per lance slot, holding which of the six command-menu entries is currently showing for that lancemate: 1 attack, 2 target, 3 follow, 4 patrol, 5 godirect, 6 shutdown, 0 none. Each lance_order_* menu entry writes its own number here beside calling lance_order_issue, and lance_order_selected reads it back, answering 7 for a slot out of range. Note the UI numbering is not the order code: the menu shows attack first, but its order code is 3 and target's is 2.

devDirEntryCount.doc: entries used in devDirEntries; project_add_entry fatal_errors with 'Too many project file entries' when it is already past 199

animPlayerError.doc: why anim_player_step gave up: 5, 4, 6 and 7 mark four different null fields in the animation record it was handed. Each is written immediately before a return of 0, which is what ties the numbers to the checks. NO READER has been found, so whether anything acts on the distinction is not established

projectPathCount.doc: how many projectPaths rows are loaded. path_table_load appends while it is below 0x40; task_object_track searches this many by name

animTrackHighest.doc: the highest animTracks slot any anim TASK has referenced: only anim_player_step raises it (to its track index + animTrackBase), and anim_ensure_loaded reads it to place the next animation. QUIRK: so the next ANIM's base follows the tracks tasks USE, not the tracks the previous ANIM LOADED - an ANIM whose last tracks no task names is overlapped by the next one, and while this is still 0 the next ANIM gets the same base. 0 in the image

animTrackBase.doc: the animTracks slot the current ANIM's track 0 sits at. anim_ensure_loaded sets it: on an animCache hit to the base saved with that animation, on a miss to animTrackHighest + 1 - only when animTrackHighest is above 0 - before res_load_anim registers the tracks at their slot + this (through anim_track_base). anim_player_step adds it to a TSK anim task's third value to find the track. 0 in the image

animCacheCount.doc: how many animCache pairs are filled, capped at 0x3c by anim_ensure_loaded - which does nothing at all once the cap is reached

objectPointInsideMethods.doc: One column of a method table indexed by WorldObject.objectClass with a stride of 0xc - three function pointers per class, six classes, spanning 0x95a5c..0x95aa0. Column 0 is the point-inside predicate: when no exact raycast method exists for a class, world_object_raycast marches four sample points along the segment and asks this one whether each is inside, stopping at the first yes - which is why those hits land on a quarter boundary rather than on the surface. The indexing is established, not inferred from spacing: world_object_raycast reads (&terrainHandlers)[objectClass * 3] for column 0 and DAT_00095a60 + objectClass * 0xc for column 1, and object_is_ground (formerly project_entry_sub_01c2e0) computes objectClass * 4 - objectClass, which is objectClass * 3, and loads [that * 4 + 0x95a64] for column 2. Same base, same stride, three columns. CORRECTION: 0x95a5c was labelled terrainHandlers and described as 11 flat slots, every target in the terrain module. Eleven is simply how many of the eighteen entries are non-null when the table is read as one flat run; the shape is 6 by 3 and the entries are per-class methods, not a list of terrain handlers.

objectRaycastMethods.doc: One column of a method table indexed by WorldObject.objectClass with a stride of 0xc - three function pointers per class, six classes, spanning 0x95a5c..0x95aa0. Column 1 is the exact raycast method, tried first by world_object_raycast and called as (object, ray). ray_hit_object_box occupies it for classes 0 and 1. A null here is what sends the class down the point-inside path in column 0.

objectGroundHeightMethods.doc: One column of a method table indexed by WorldObject.objectClass with a stride of 0xc - three function pointers per class, six classes, spanning 0x95a5c..0x95aa0. Column 2 is the GROUND-HEIGHT method: called with (object, x, y, z, &height), it reports the height of that object's walkable surface under (x, z). world_find_highest_hit and world_ground_height_near are its callers, and only classes 0 and 5 have one - class 5's is walkmesh_ground_height (formerly terrain_sub_01ef90), which searches the object's quadtree (+0x44) and mesh (+0x1c) for the polygon underfoot. object_is_ground tests it for null. RENAMED from objectMethod2: the old note said 'what it does is not established', which was true until its two callers were read.

hitNormalX.doc: x of the surface normal at the last raycast hit. The three are established as one vector rather than three scalars because project_entry hands them to vec3_normalise as a triple. ray_hit_object_box writes them as a unit axis - plus or minus 0x10000 on whichever of the three slabs the ray entered through, signed against the ray direction - and other hit paths derive them from a plane instead

hitNormalY.doc: y of the same normal - see hitNormalX

groundNormalX.doc: x of the surface normal under the last ground-height query, 16.16. world_ground_height_near and world_find_highest_hit copy hitNormalX/Y/Z here for the surface they choose. mech_std_tick_terrain is the consumer: it takes groundNormalX * headingSin + groundNormalZ * headingCos - the slope along the mech's direction of travel - and when that exceeds slopeThreshold either way it adds gravity * slope * tickDelta to the forward speed ramp (ramps[2].current), so a mech gains speed downhill and loses it uphill

groundNormalY.doc: y of the same normal - see groundNormalX

groundNormalZ.doc: z of the same normal - see groundNormalX

rayHitNormalX.doc: x of the surface normal at the nearest hit of the last world_raycast or world_raycast_no_mechs, 16.16 - they copy hitNormalX/Y/Z here for the hit they keep

rayHitNormalY.doc: y of the same normal. ai_handle_blocked's consumer fixes the WALKABLE SLOPE: a probe hit on an object for which object_is_ground is true, with this at or above 0xc41b, is not an obstacle. 0xc41b is cos(40 degrees) in 16.16 (50203.5), so ground up to 40 degrees steep is walkable. A hit on the destructibles family (type & 0xf0 == 0x50) is not an obstacle either

rayHitNormalZ.doc: z of the same normal - see rayHitNormalX

groundQuadtreesDisabled.doc: while non-zero, object_build_ground_quadtree builds nothing, so class-5 objects get no quadtree at +0x44. Only disable_ground_quadtrees sets it, and only the command-line parser in check_launched_by_shell calls that, so it is a startup switch. Which switch letter is not established

renormCountdownSeed.doc: the next value handed to a SceneNode's renormCountdown (see that field). scene_node_create, scene_node_init_in_place and scene_node_rotate_local (on renormalising) each copy it into the node and advance it to ((old + 7) & 0x7f) + 0x40. Six of its eight absolute-address uses are in those three; the other two (0x1e048, 0x1e05c) are in an UNRECOVERED routine at 0x1e020..0x1e06b that composes a node's local transform with the one in EDX (transform_compose), sets the +0x74 dirty bit and does the same countdown and reseed - but nothing calls it or points at it, so it is dead. 100 in the data, so the sequence runs 100, 171, 114, 185, 128, 71, 142, 85, ... and every value after the first is in 64..191: a node is renormalised every 64 to 191 incremental rotations, staggered so neighbouring nodes do not renormalise on the same frame

scroungeTileSize.doc: the grid pitch the scrounge patch is snapped to, in world units (cm). scrounge_install takes the larger of the patch mesh's x and z extents - the whole extent if the node has children, a third of it otherwise - and rounds it up to the next multiple of 0x4000 (163.84 m). scrounge_follow_viewer divides viewerPosition's x and z by it to get the cell under the camera

scroungeActive.doc: scrounge_follow_viewer does nothing while this is 0. scrounge_install sets it; scrounge_detach clears it

scroungeHysteresis.doc: set when the scrounge node has children (SceneNode.firstChild). scrounge_follow_viewer then leaves the patch where it is until the camera is more than 0.5625 x scroungeTileSize ((size >> 3) + size) >> 1, 0xf43ac) from its origin on either axis, and rounds the new cell to the nearest rather than flooring. Clear, it re-snaps on every cell change

scroungeNode.doc: the scene node of the mission object named by the SCRG chunk. scrounge_install takes it out of the world; scrounge_follow_viewer re-origins it at (cellX * scroungeTileSize, 0, cellZ * scroungeTileSize) whenever the camera's cell changes, and re-walks it

worldRoot.doc: head of the world object chain, linked through +0x10 with the back link at +0x0c. This is a separate membership from the scene tree's parent/child links: world_find_highest_hit walks this chain, and object_remove_from_world takes an object out of it without freeing it or detaching its node.

altRoot.doc: pointer to altRootNode, set beside worldRoot by the same initialiser. hud_debug hands it to a tree walk, which is the only other thing that reads it

monoObjectivesTable.doc: which objective table the monochrome debug monitor shows (objective_debug_view): AI_n_MONO_OBJECTIVES (0x65..0x6e) set it to n, or -1 when n is not below missionTableCount; OBJECTIVES_OFF (0x6f) switches it between -1 and -2. The FAIL/SUCCEED_MONO_OBJECTIVE debug commands act on objectiveTables[this]

monoObjectiveSelected.doc: the objective selected in that view: NEXT_MONO_OBJECTIVE / PREV_MONO_OBJECTIVE (0x70/0x71) step it; FAIL_MONO_OBJECTIVE (0x72) forces that objective from state 3 (in progress) to 6 (failed) - a developer switch for forcing mission results

aiStateNames.doc: the game's own name/value table for MechEntity.aiState: 13 pairs of {char *name, int value} terminated by a null pointer. nothing -1, idle 0, avoid 1, target 2, attack 3, flee 4, follow 5, recon 6, patrol 7, godirect 8, rest 10, shutdown 11, dead 12 - 9 is not in the table. This is the table that makes the AI readable, and it is also a warning: walking the strings forward instead of reading the pointers gives 'flee' and 'follow' as one spliced entry, which is why listing/strings.txt shows '_PRfollow' at 0x9044d. The name beside each value is the game's, not ours.

aiStateNamesShort.doc: 13 {name, value} records, the three-letter forms of aiStateNames for the debug overlay - nil -1, idl 0, avd 1, tgt 2, atk 3, fle 4, fol 5, rec 6, ptl 7, god 8, res 10, shu 11, ded 12. It sits immediately after the 14-record long table at 0x95bd0 and agrees with it value for value, including skipping 9.

targetDesignatorNames.doc: 7 {name, value} records naming the symbolic target designators the mission data uses in place of a real object handle: agp_user 0x2200, agp_myleader 0x2201, agp_me 0x2202, agp_home 0x2100, agp_rbanchor 0x2101, agp_friendly 0x4200 and agp_enemy 0x4201. ai_apply_state prints the target through it. These are what the AI logs show for a target that is a role rather than an object - and they explain ai_try_enter_state's one special case, state 5 with target 0x2201, which reads as follow with my leader as the target.

handleTypeLetters.doc: 3 {name, value} records giving a one-letter tag for the type half of an object handle, looked up as (handle >> 8 & 0xf) << 8: n 0x100, p 0x200, t 0x400. Those are the tracked-object, mech and gamething types in MechEntity.targetPrimary's encoding.

altTypeLetters.doc: 3 one-letter type tags read off the object type word at +2 of a scene node userdata, as (word >> 8 & 0xf) << 8: p 0x100, t 0x200, r 0x800. The debug overlay uses it on MechEntity.avoidObstacle, so these letters tag the KIND of obstacle a mech is steering round. RESOLVED - an earlier pass recorded the values but said which kind each letter stands for was not established, and warned that this table must not be read with handleTypeLetters' meanings. The first half of that warning can now go: p IS mech and t IS gamething, the same two things those same two letters mean in handleTypeLetters. The second half stands, because the VALUES still differ - the object word carries each type one bit LOWER than a handle does. Mech is 0x200 in a handle and 0x100 here; gamething is 0x400 there and 0x200 here. Two routes agree. projectile_update dispatches impact damage on this word: bit 0x100 takes the index at +0x14 as a mechTable slot and calls mech_apply_damage on that mech's loadout, bit 0x200 calls gamething_apply_damage on the object itself, and a nibble of 0x50 in bits 4-7 calls destructible_apply_damage with the same +0x14 index. Separately mech_has_line_of_fire decides whether a raycast hit is the thing a mech was aiming at by pairing object bit 0x100 with handle type 2 and object bit 0x200 with handle type 4 - the same shift, arrived at independently. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: what r at 0x800 is, and what bit 0x400 selects - projectile_update only uses it to choose between setting impactFlags bit 1 and bit 2 on a hit that is neither mech nor gamething nor destructible.

gamepieceClassNames.doc: 8 {name, value} records naming the gamepiece classes, i.e. the values of GamepieceClass.classId and MechEntity.gamepieceClass (formerly objectState): GP_NULL 0, GP_MW2MECH 1, GP_MW2TRUCK 2, GP_MW2ARTILLERY 3, GP_MW2TANK 4, GP_MW2HELICOPTER 5, GP_MW2WANDERER 6, GP_MW2DOOR 7. UNREFERENCED: no code immediate and no data pointer anywhere in the image reaches it or any entry in it (checked for every dword in 0x95d28..0x95d78), unlike its neighbours targetDesignatorNames and mechStatusNames, which the AI log functions use. So it is dead data in the shipped build. It is trusted because the GP chunks in MW2.PRJ agree with it class by class - see MechEntity.gamepieceClass (formerly objectState). Class 8 has no entry. The records before it at 0x95ce8, 0x95d00 and 0x95d18 are three small handle-type name tables ('nv'/'gp'/'gt', 'n'/'p'/'t', 'p'/'t'/'r'); ai_debug_mech_table (formerly ai_log_invalid_target) and 0x512ef use them

mechStatusNames.doc: 8 {name, value} records for MechLoadout.status, two letters each: of 0, su 1, nm 2, sd 3, dd 4, ej 5, co 6, ds 7. Read as off, startup, normal, shutdown, dead, eject - which is the game confirming most of what the status comment had already worked out from behaviour, correcting 0 from "just spawned" to simply off, and identifying 5 as ejection. What co and ds stand for is NOT established; nothing in the game produces or tests status 6 or 7 (see MechLoadout.status for the sweep that settles it).

taskTypeNames.doc: 15 {name, value} records whose values are single bits - non 0, ann 1, des 2, def 4, rec 8, beg 0x10, ret 0x20, sur 0x40, end 0x80, got 0x100, wai 0x200, sle 0x400, shu 0x800, xpl 0x1000, lev 0x2000 - so the field they name is a bitmask, not an enum. The AI debug overlay reads it from +2 of a record it is handed, and the project file has a TSK/task chunk, which is where the name comes from. Expanding the abbreviations (announce, destroy, defend, recon...) is guesswork and is NOT established.

aiBehaviourNames.doc: 14 {name, value} records of 8 bytes, the game's own names for the values of MechEntity.aiBehaviour, read through lookup_name_by_value by the AI debug overlay. Six-character padded: stupid 0, behind 1, achick 2, asrp 3, ajmpin 4, adfa 5, kama 6, wchick 7, wbackp 8, wpeek 9, avoid 10, sprint 11, circle 12, and a blank for -1. The same shape as aiStateNames at 0x95bd0, and dumped the same way - reading that one back reproduces the state names already recorded for aiState, including the absence of 9, which is what vouches for this table being read correctly.

aiRuleSelectState1.doc: short pairs read when MechEntity.gamepieceClass (formerly objectState) is 1: [ruleIndex][0 = this mech leads its group, 1 = it does not] gives an aiRuleTables slot. The six arrays from here to aiRuleSelectState6 are one per gamepieceClass value and are only ever read by ai_set_state_rule_block. All six are byte-for-byte identical in the shipped binary: 15 [leader, follower] pairs, decoded with the rules themselves in tools/dump_ai_rules.py

aiRuleSelectState5.doc: the gamepieceClass 5 array, and gamepieceClass 8 reads the same one - see aiRuleSelectState1

cheatFriendlyAllies.doc: 0 in the image; toggled by the cheat 'lairdo' (cheat_handle_command, message 'ATTENTION ENEMIES: Don't mess with the blimp.'), its only writer. Its one reader is the agp_friendly (0x4200) walk in resolve_target_designator. Normally that yields only mechs whose group leader is playerMechIndex, the player's own lance. With this set, it also yields any mech whose mech_allegiance is 0, so every mech on the player's side counts as friendly for the AI rules that use agp_friendly. Named for that effect; what the blimp message refers to is not established

aiTargetUnclaimedFirst.doc: 1 in the image and NEVER WRITTEN: a sweep of every function finds only two reads, in ai_rule_cond_team_target and ai_state_target_unclaimed, and no pointer to it anywhere in the image. ai_rule_cond_team_target returns ai_find_target_unclaimed's nearest-UNCLAIMED answer when it is non-zero and the plain nearest when it is zero, so in the shipped game AI mechs always prefer an enemy no squadmate has taken - lances spread their fire. The zero branch is dead. Presumably a compile-time or debug switch; nothing establishes that

aiStateHandlers.doc: the AI state machine's jump table, indexed directly by MechEntity.aiState. Most slots share one default handler and only a few states have their own, which is why ai_run_combat_state only bothers to switch on cases 2, 3 and 6. Called as aiStateHandlers[mech->aiState](mech, (short)targetPrimary) by mech_ai_think (formerly mission_log_sub_021510) for AI-controlled mechs when ai_rules_run returned 0. THE SLOTS, read from the data and mapped by aiStateNames: 13 of them, 0..12. ai_state_hold serves 0 idle and 11 shutdown; ai_state_attack serves 3 attack; ai_state_move serves 1, 2 and 4..10; slot 12 (dead) is null and the dispatcher skips aiState 12. aiRuleConditions begins straight after, at 0x96050, which is what fixes this table at 13 slots.

aiRuleConditions.doc: 8 slots, indexed by short [0] of an AI rule record. These are not boolean predicates - each one searches for something and returns an object handle, or 0 for nothing found, and ai_rules_run passes that handle straight on to the rule's action. Slot 0 is null. Slot 4 returns its own first operand unchanged, i.e. a literal, and slot 5 always returns 0. Slot 1 is the one read in full: it sweeps candidates with resolve_target_designator (formerly ai_state_sub_022f00), validates each through ai_validate_current_target and keeps the nearest inside a range of operand * 100, with -3 meaning no limit. The table runs to 0x9606c and aiRuleActions begins immediately after, which is what fixes it at 8 entries.

aiRuleActions.doc: 5 slots, indexed by the low byte of short [3] of an AI rule record, and called with the mech, the record and whatever handle the rule's condition returned. Slot 0 does nothing but return 1. Slot 1 zeroes pendingCount. Slot 2 packs aiState and targetSecondary into one dword at +0x124, the pending queue's first slot, and sets pendingCount to 1 if it was 0 - it saves what the mech was doing. Slot 3 is the matching pop: it decrements pendingCount and hands the entry to ai_try_enter_state. Slot 4 is ai_rule_post_to_leader. Slots 5 and up are null, which is what fixes it at 5 entries.

mechCount.doc: upper bound on valid mech indices; guards every mechTable lookup. THE CAP IS 60: project_chunk_exec's GP branch compares it with 0x3c before spawning (cmp ecx, 0x3c / jge 0x4fbdd at 0x4edff) and, at 60 or more, jumps to the function's exit - so every chunk left in that stream, not just the gamepiece, is dropped, with no system_error report. A port that allows more gamepieces changes what the later chunks of an overfull mission file do

gameThingCount.doc: bumped by gamething_alloc, which refuses beyond 254

autoEjectEnabled.doc: the Automatic ejection option, 0 in the image. command_execute (formerly option_toggle)'s case 0x3c flips it and posts 'Automatic ejection ON' / 'OFF' - only when the player's mech has MechEntity.flags bit 0x2000 - and the options screen code at 0x19ab0/0x19b20 reads and restores it. Its two sim readers, mech_heat_meltdown and mech_damage_slot, both set the loadout's status to 5, the ejection sequence, before a mech is destroyed when it is set - or always for a mech that is not the player's

enemyArmorScale.doc: the multiplier on section armour for every mech mech_allegiance calls non-zero - enemy (1) or neutral (2) - set from SimOptions.difficulty: 1 at level 0, 3 at level 1, 4 at level 2 (0x4c79a..0x4c7e3). So level 0 is the easiest, and at level 2 every side gets the player's 4. Friendly AI mechs use a third factor that mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config) keeps in a local (friendlyArmorScale: 3, 3, 4). THE GAME DIVIDES INCONSISTENTLY: mech_apply_damage divides every non-player mech's armour by THIS scale, friendly ones included, so at level 0 a friendly mech's damage level is computed as if it had 3x the armour it does. Recorded as the game's behaviour, not corrected

playerArmorScale.doc: the multiplier on the PLAYER mech's section armour. mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config) sets it from SimOptions.difficulty (4 at every level) and multiplies armorFront and armorRear of all eight sections by it before the << 16 to 16.16 (0x4ca8e..0x4cad4, the branch taken when entity->index == playerMechIndex). Internal structure is never scaled. The consumers divide it back out to get chassis-file units: mech_apply_damage for the player, and hud_damage_diagram_draw (formerly damage_sub_02f560) and netplay's two damage-level expressions for any mech, all computing 15 - 3 * (internal + armour / scale) / (max << 16)

heatWarningLatch.doc: 1 once the player has heard the 66-percent 'Heat level critical' warning (cue 0, sound 0xe9 MECOVHW1); mech_heat_update sets it with the time in heatWarningTick and only while heat is rising, and clears it after 0x2d8 ticks (4 s) back below 66

jetClimbLimit.doc: caps how fast jump jets can climb. While the jets fire and velocityY is positive, mech_std_tick_terrain adds (gravity - jetDeltaY) * 0xe38 * velocityY >> 16 / this to the vertical acceleration (0x26d42..0x26d79; the 0xe38 = 3640 is built as x*7*8*65). With the jets' own (jetDeltaY - gravity), the net upward acceleration is (jetDeltaY - gravity) * (1 - f), where f = 3640 * velocityY / (65536 * this). It falls to zero at f = 1 WHATEVER THE THRUST OR GRAVITY, so this fixes a terminal climb speed of this * 65536 / 3640 in 16.16 cm per tick - at 182 ticks a second, exactly this / 20 cm/s. Default 100000 (50 m/s); the PLNT chunk's word 10 overrides it when positive, and the 46 shipped planets use 1000 to 100000, 0.5 to 50 m/s (first recorded as 1000 to 70000 from a byte scan that saw a different set of records - see the correction on gravity). The thrust itself still decides how quickly a mech approaches that speed

slopeThreshold.doc: the slope, as a 16.16 normal component along the heading, below which ground slope does not change a mech's speed - see groundNormalX. Default 0x2000 (0.125, about 7.2 degrees); the PLNT (planet) chunk overrides it from its dword 0xd when that is positive, in the same handler that sets gravity and ambientTemperature. In the shipped data 19 of the 46 PLNT records set 0x10000 (first recorded as 20 of 49 - see the correction on gravity), which no 16.16 normal component can exceed, so on those worlds slope never changes speed; 15 leave it 0 and get the default

cheatInfiniteJumpjets.doc: 1 while the jump-jet fuel cheat is on: cheat_handle_command toggles it, posting 'Infinite Jumpjet juice ON' / 'OFF'; its one reader, mech_std_tick_ai, then does not burn the PLAYER's jumpFuel while the jets fire

jettisonAmmoRequest.doc: cleared by mech_std_tick_player (formerly mech_std_tick_weapons), which then calls weapon_jettison_ammo.

mascToggleRequest.doc: set by the input layer, cleared by mech_std_tick_player (formerly mech_std_tick_weapons). When MechLoadout.flags lacks bit 0x10 the answer is the message 'Not equipped with MASC'.

mascEngaged.doc: whether MASC is running. mech_std_tick_player (formerly mech_std_tick_weapons) toggles it on a request, playing sound 0xcb on and 0xca off, and the MASC malfunction path in the AI tick clears it while adding a quarter to heatLevel - which is what confirms it rather than the sounds.

playerOut.doc: RENAMED from playerEjectedDone: it is set on the player's DEATH too, so it means the player is out of the mission, killed or ejected. The status-4 branch of mech_std_tick_player writes 1 on the first tick of destruction (mov edx, 1 at 0x283c1, kept across death_flash, stored at 0x283d2) - the 'register noise' below was a preservation artefact, resolved once death_flash was known to keep EDX. Original note: becomes 1 when the player mech's status-5 sequence (the 0x38e-tick ejection timer, per MechLoadout.status) runs out, in mech_std_tick_player (formerly mech_std_tick_weapons). The status < 5 branch also writes it, with a value from register noise that has not been untangled. (RESOLVED - it writes 1; see the start of this note.) mission_results_update fails the player's still-undecided table (result 3) once it is set, and the camera code in geom_luma branches on it throughout. The name assumes the status-5 reading of the ejection sequence is right

reactorRequest.doc: the player's manual reactor control, and a three-state one: -1 shuts down, +1 powers up, 0 idle. Shutdown plays cue 0xd and sound 0xf2 and forces MechLoadout.status to 3; startup posts 'Powering up...', sets status to 0 and clears bit 0x10 of MechEntity.flags. Both are the same states the heat ladder drives, reached deliberately instead of by overheating.

lastPlayerHeading.doc: the player mech's heading at the end of the previous mech_std_tick_ai, written there every tick; the only reader is the alignLegsToTorso step, which subtracts it from the current heading to get this tick's turn

mascLastRollTick.doc: when the MASC malfunction was last rolled. The rule, in full: while mascEngaged and at most once per 0xb6 ticks, random_range(0x3c) has to come up exactly 0xc - one in sixty - with the mech running and the option byte clear. The hit posts 'MASC malfunction', plays sound 0xc9, adds a quarter to heatLevel and switches MASC off.

hudEnabled.doc: whether the cockpit HUD is drawn. command_execute case 0x13, TOGGLE_HUD (F11 in GAMEKEY.MAP), flips it; 1 in the data. Read by the per-frame HUD dispatcher player_cockpit_frame (formerly sound_res_sub_032c50) - which only copies playerStatusCopy while it is set - and by the vfx_video, ui_callbacks and ai_group HUD routines

trackedObjectCount.doc: live entries in trackedObjects; the creator refuses beyond 128

playerTargetFromReticle.doc: 1 once the player has taken a target through the target reticle, 0 once they cycle targets. player_target_reticle sets it (both on its null-crosshair exit and after a retarget); ai_cycle_target clears it when the mech is the player. CONSUMERS, the three validators, only when the attacker is the player: while it is 0, ai_validate_target refuses (-3) a mech whose flags has 0x10, and ai_validate_target and ai_validate_gamething refuse (-5) a target whose flags high byte has neither bit of 0x14. So target CYCLING skips those targets while pointing the reticle at one takes it anyway. What those bits mean was not established when this was written; it now is, on MechEntity.flags: 0x10 is powered down by the AI (rest/shutdown), and 0x400 / 0x1000 mark a combatant - so cycling skips powered-down mechs and non-combatants such as doors. 0 in the data

playerGroupIndex.doc: the group the player flies with. group_set_formation compares its argument against this to decide whether the formation change is worth announcing on the radio, and the lance menu passes it to lance_get_formation and lance_set_formation as the group to act on.

formationCount.doc: how many formationPresets rows are actually loaded; the only bound group_set_formation_by_name searches within.

fallingObjectCount.doc: how many fallingObjects slots are in use. falling_object_attach bumps it and the release path decrements it, and nothing else touches it, so it is a live count rather than a running total.

probeDirections.doc: 16 {dx, dz} pairs of dwords, one per compass point in 22.5-degree steps, clockwise from straight ahead: 0 is (0, 1), 4 is (1, 0), 8 is (0, -1), 12 is (-1, 0). The entries are DIVISORS, not components: mech_probe_ray computes length / dx and length / dz and leaves a 0 entry as 0. So point 1, (2, 1), gives (L/2, L), which is atan(1/2) = 26.6 degrees rather than 22.5, and the diagonal gives (L, L). The directions are approximate, and the probes are longer off the axes, up to L * 1.41. Directly followed by 6.0 and 1.0 in 16.16, which belong to something else. CORRECTION, from typeBehaviourTransitions: they do - read as shorts, 0x963f4 is (0, 6, 0, 1 ...), the first row of behaviourTransitionsMech, not a 16.16 pair

aiBehaviourSetsReady.doc: 0 until ai_behaviour_init first fills aiBehaviourSets and aiBehaviourSetElemental, then 1

damageDiagramSections.doc: int[16]: the section each region of the damage diagram shows, as the 1-based location mech_apply_damage takes. hud_damage_diagram_draw reads loadout->sections[damageDiagramSections[i] - 1] for region i. Contents: 1, 3, 3, 2, 2, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 0 - the head once, then two regions each for centre torso, right torso, left torso, right arm, left arm, right leg and left leg (location names from debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section)). Both regions of a pair get the same colour, since the level is the larger of front and rear, so the pair is not front/rear; what separates them is in the region rectangles, which are not decoded. The final 0 would index sections[-1]

targetDisplayMode.doc: the target display's mode: command_execute case 8, TOGGLE_TARGET_DISPLAY (F4), steps it 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0; 1 in the data. Its consumer, hud_widget13_tick (the target view), draws nothing while it is 0, draws the target in wireframe (wireframeMode 1, colour scheme 0) at 1, and without wireframe at 2

objectivesDisplayOn.doc: whether the objectives display is shown: hud_objectives_draw returns at once while it is 0. Its only writer is command_execute case 0x41, DISPLAY_OBJECTIVES (F12 in GAMEKEY.MAP), which flips it; 0 in the data, so the display starts hidden

objectivesDisplayTable.doc: which objectiveTables entry the objectives display lists - read by hud_objectives_draw and objectives_draw_category, and NEVER WRITTEN: its three absolute-address references are all reads, and it is 0 in the data. So the display always shows table 0, which is the player's group's: all 16 player gamepieces in MW2.PRJ are in group 0 (listing/gamepieces.txt)

punchInAutoHeadingRequest.doc: RENAMED from faceLegsToTorsoRequest: command 0x4c is PUNCH_IN_AUTO_HDG in commandNames. A one-shot request: command_execute (formerly option_toggle) case 0x4c (a player command) sets it to 1, and player_cockpit_frame (formerly sound_res_sub_032c50) clears it on its next frame, first calling mech_punch_in_auto_heading (formerly mech_face_legs_to_torso) on the player's loadout if playerStatusCopy is 2 (running). Those are its only three references

playerHitFlashPending.doc: a one-frame request for the damage flash, 0 in the image. Two writers set it to 1: mech_apply_damage, for a hit on the PLAYER's location 1 or 3 (head or centre torso) of more than 0x20000 (2 armour points) that reaches internal structure while status is not 4; and mech_damage_slot, when a destroyed slot of the player's still holds rounds (an ammo explosion). The one reader, cockpit_status_sounds (formerly sound_res_sub_032fc0) (the per-frame cockpit update), clears it, bumps playerHitFlashCount and calls damage_flash(playerHitFlashCount * 3)

cockpitLastStatus.doc: the player's MechLoadout.status as cockpit_status_sounds last saw it; a status change plays SNDS 0xf6 on entering 0 or 4 and 0xce on entering 2

lockedToneLatch.doc: 1 once cockpit_status_sounds has played the LOCKED tone (MECXLOCK) for the current lock; reset whenever MechLoadout.flags bit 0x80 is clear

lockToneLatch.doc: 1 once cockpit_status_sounds has played the lock-countdown tone for the current countdown; it follows MechLoadout.flags bit 0x40 back to 0 when no countdown runs, so the tone plays once per attempt

playerHitFlashCount.doc: how many damage flashes this run has shown, 0 in the image. Only cockpit_status_sounds (formerly sound_res_sub_032fc0) touches it - one read and one write, its only relocations - and it is never reset, so from the fifth severe hit on every flash is the full two seconds

cacheBuckets.doc: the resource cache hash table: 1009 (0x3f1, a prime) bucket heads of CacheItem chains, from cache_table_create's calloc(0x3f1, 4). Every user computes the bucket the same way: (id + the four type bytes) % 0x3f1. cache_lookup, cache_free_item and cache_load_resource all agree on it

frameArenaBytes.doc: size of the per-frame arena, arenaKB << 10 from render_buffers_init - 0x20000 in the game

renderBuffers.doc: the single block render_buffers_init gets from cache_alloc: frameArenaBytes of per-frame arena, then polyDrawList and walkDrawList (drawListCapacity 8-byte entries each). It zeroes it with cache_memset and copies it to frameArenaBase and frameArenaLow; render_buffers_free is the only other user, freeing it through cache_dealloc at video shutdown. Typed byte * so the arithmetic on it reads in bytes

arenaBlockCount.doc: how many arenaBlocks static_arena_init has opened; it fatal_errors on opening a sixth

arenaTagCount.doc: how many arenaTags entries are live. static_arena_init zeroes it, static_arena_reserve appends and fatal_errors past 0x20, static_malloc searches up to it

fileStatus.doc: why the last file_size, file_load or file_save failed. Zero on entry to each, then 2 for an allocation failure, 3 for a failed open or size query, 4 for a failed open or write on the save path, 5 for a short read, 6 for a short write. Two of file_load's stores print as register noise in the exported source; the disassembly at 0x354c3 and 0x354e9 gives them as 3 and 5. NOTHING READS IT - all twelve occurrences across the three functions are writes, so whether anything was ever meant to consume it is not established

detailMapValues.doc: pointer to detail-record indices, parallel to detailMapIds. An outermost REPR fills detailMapCapacity entries with -1

detailMapIds.doc: pointer to the mangled ids of the detail map; parallel to detailMapValues and bounded by detailMapCount

projectReprActive.doc: non-zero while a REPR..ENDR group is open. RENAMED from projectRepeatActive. CORRECTION: REPR is not a repeat. Neither REPR nor ENDR touches the chunk reader, so nothing between them runs twice; what the flag changes is project_obj_exec, which while it is set records each OBJ's POLY id as a detail level through detail_record_set instead of loading the mesh. An outermost REPR also empties the detail map (detailMapCount = 0, every detailMapValues entry -1). The keyword 'rep' reads as REPResentation

projectReprLevel.doc: which detail level the OBJ chunks inside a REPR describe: 0 at the outermost REPR, +1 for each nested one. RENAMED from projectRepeatDepth - the counting was described correctly, the meaning was not. project_obj_exec passes it as the level argument of detail_record_set, which stores the POLY id in slot [2 + level] of the object's record, and mech_apply_detail_level later loads slot [2 + level] for the level it is asked for. So a REPR nest is a list of successively coarser meshes for one object id, and a port that implements REPR as a loop gets every model wrong. The exported source prints the reset as projectReprLevel = projectReprActive, which looks like a copy but is not - the decompiler knows that flag is zero on that branch and substituted it for the constant

worldRecordMapValues.doc: pointer to world-object record indices, parallel to worldRecordMapIds. The first BLK at depth zero resets worldRecordMapCapacity entries of it to -1

worldRecordMapIds.doc: pointer to the mangled ids of the world record map; parallel to worldRecordMapValues

projectObjectCount.doc: entries in projectObjectMap. project_object_register appends while it is below projectObjectCapacity; project_object_find searches down from it

projectObjectCapacity.doc: the bound project_object_register checks projectObjectCount against

projectObjectMap.doc: pointer to 8-byte {mangled id, WorldObject *} records - the stride is fixed by both project_object_register and project_object_find indexing at count * 8 and reading the value at +4. Every mesh an OBJ chunk loads outside a REPR or BLK is registered here, and POS, ROT and the parent lookup read it back

worldObjectCount.doc: bound on GameThing.geomIndex and on every other index into worldRecords (0x101e90 - CORRECTED from 0x101e9c, which was the right stride counted from the wrong base). Worth knowing that the two guards disagree by one: world_object_node and world_record_object (formerly geom_poly_sub_0367c0) accept index < count, world_object_get_pos accepts index <= count.

worldRecordsReady.doc: 0 until world_record_alloc first runs, which resets all 0x402 world-object records and sets it

projectBlockNextSlot.doc: the next free slot in projectBlockFrames. project_block_begin fills this slot, makes it projectBlockCurrent and increments it; slots are never handed back, which is why the frames are indexed by slot and not by depth

projectBlockCurrent.doc: the frame slot of the innermost open BLK, or -1 outside any. project_block_begin sets it to the slot it just filled and project_block_end restores it from projectBlockStack. block_transform_point reads it to put a point into that frame, and project_obj_exec's in-block path requires it to be set

projectBlockDepth.doc: how many project-file blocks are open. project_block_begin raises it on BLK, project_block_end lowers it on ENDB and calls system_error if it goes negative, so the file is trusted to balance its own blocks

pendingBlockXform.doc: nine dwords a BLKX chunk leaves for the next BLK: block_xform_set writes them, project_block_begin copies them into the new frame at +0x24 and then refills them from defaultBlockXform, so each BLKX applies to one block. The nine dwords are (integer scale x3, pitch, yaw, roll in 16.16 degrees, x, y, z in cm), the OBJ record's layout; the scale is dead in project_block_begin, which builds a scale matrix and never uses it

defaultBlockXform.doc: the nine dwords pendingBlockXform is reset to after every BLK; only read. The nine dwords are (integer scale x3, pitch, yaw, roll in 16.16 degrees, x, y, z in cm), the OBJ record's layout; the scale is dead in project_block_begin, which builds a scale matrix and never uses it

debrisEnabled.doc: 1 in the image. While it is 0, world_record_build refuses every record whose GameThing carries flag 0x8000 (DEBRIS), so wrecked structures leave no loose pieces. Written only by debris_set_enabled, one of the detail options ui_callbacks_sub_019bb0 applies from the block at *0x97e3c (its +0x24); read by world_record_build and by debris_enabled, which nothing calls

detailRecordCount.doc: records in use in the 0x44-stride detail table at 0x120fa0, at most 0x30c. detail_record_set takes the next one for a level-0 OBJ; mech_apply_detail_level scans this many

detailRecordsReady.doc: 0 until detail_record_set first runs detail_records_reset, which sets it

bitmap3dNeedsReset.doc: -2 in the image, so the first BMPJ of a run calls bitmap3d_reset, which sets it to 0

lumaTableId.doc: the LUMA resource the mission uses as its shade table. project_chunk_exec's LTBL case sets it from the chunk: the id, or when that is -1 the name looked up through resource_id_by_name(0xd), which is LUMTABLE with FOG, STANDARD and TRAINING. bitmap3d_draw loads it into lumaTable the first time it needs it

bitmap3dCurrentBlock.doc: the bitmap3dFrames block that BMPJ chunks with no explicit block append to. bitmap3d_add_frame advances it by one when bitmap3dAdvancePending is set; bitmap3d_set_id binds a slot to it. So in a mission stream a run of BMPJ chunks fills one block with frames, a BMID binds a 3dbitmap slot to that block, and the next BMPJ starts a new block

bitmap3dAdvancePending.doc: set by bitmap3d_set_id when it binds a slot to the current block, cleared by bitmap3d_add_frame as it moves to the next block

lumaTable.doc: the cached LUMA shade table: cache_load_resource(mainProject, lumaTableId, 'LUMA'), loaded once by bitmap3d_draw and never unlocked there. What the table's bytes map, colour and shade level to colour presumably, is read by the rasteriser, which is out of scope, and is not established

skyColour.doc: the fill colour render_sky_and_ground passes for the above-horizon region, always in the branch skyEnabled guards. A palette INDEX, 224 in the image. The SKYM chunk can set it, but MW2.PRJ has no SKYM chunk in any BWD stream, so every mission uses 224 and the colour itself comes from the mission palette (PALG). The horizon band shades from here to groundColour - 1

groundColour.doc: the below-horizon fill colour, always in the branch groundEnabled guards. A palette INDEX, 239 in the image. Like skyColour it is never overridden, because MW2.PRJ has no GNDM chunk, so the sky-to-ground ramp is always palette entries 224..238

hrzmChunkValue.doc: where the HRZM chunk puts its +8 dword, and nothing else. WRITE-ONLY: the store at 0x4e982 in project_chunk_exec is the only reference in the image. 0 in all 34 HRZM chunks, 234 in the image. Named for where it comes from because no reader gives it a meaning, the same as climChunkValue

damageShadeRaises.doc: PLNT record [15] (project_chunk_exec copies it verbatim). 0: a damaged mech or destructible part has its shade scaled down by (16 - level) / 16; non-zero: moved up towards 15 by level / 15 of the remaining gap (polygon_resolve_colour, 0x38e38). 15 is the fully lit end of a ramp, but whether that end is bright on a given world depends on its palette, which was not checked. 16 of the 46 PLNT records in MW2.PRJ set 1 (BRON, CHED, COLB, CYAN, FUCH, FUC2, GOUD, JACK, PROV, PUCE, RED_, SWIS, TAUP, UMBE, WHIZ, YELL *PLT1), counted with dump_objectives' chunk walker

camOrbitDistance.doc: the orbit camera's distance from its subject, in cm. camera_orbit_update seeds it at 3 x mechTable[0]'s radius on first use (0 means not yet sized), adds the player's track_distance_delta each frame and clamps it to camOrbitDistanceMin..camOrbitDistanceMax

camOrbitDistanceMax.doc: 12 x mechTable[0]'s radius; see camOrbitDistance. camOrbitHeightMax is seeded from it

camOrbitHeight.doc: the orbit camera's height above the subject's eye, in cm: seeded at a quarter of the first distance, then clamped each frame to camOrbitHeightMin..camOrbitHeightMax as camera_orbit_update adds the player's height input

camOrbitAngle.doc: the orbit camera's angle around its subject, 16.16 degrees mod 0x1680000. camera_orbit_update adds the pan input (or the post-ejection spin) each frame and places the camera at (subject yaw - this) around the subject

cameraZoomPlayer.doc: a zoom level in the 16.16 scale Viewer.zoom uses, so 0x10000 is unity. geom_luma_part1 assigns it from playerControls.zoom_factor - a channel named by the game's own control table - which is what identifies it as a zoom rather than the pointer Ghidra types it as. camera_apply_zoom picks between this and cameraZoomAlt and writes the winner to Viewer.zoom

cameraZoomAlt.doc: the second zoom level camera_apply_zoom can choose, selected when the global at 0x96ee8 is non-zero. CAUTION: every write to it that has been read sets it to 0x10000, unity, so what varies it - if anything does - is NOT established; it is named for its position beside cameraZoomPlayer in the same two-way choice

cameraModePrev.doc: the camera mode camera_update ran last frame; it stores the mode after dispatching. camera_orbit_update treats a value other than 1 as 'just entered' and re-seeds its ramps from the current view

cameraModeBeforeMissile.doc: the cameraMode camera_missile_view restores when the missile camera ends

cameraMode.doc: which camera camera_update runs: 0 and 6 -> camera_cockpit_view (formerly geom_luma_sub_039b30); 1 -> camera_orbit_update, fed the track_distance, track_height and eyepoint_pan controls; 2, and anything unlisted -> camera_free_fly, fed track_height, track_distance, eyepoint_slide, eyepoint_pan and eyepoint_tilt; 3 -> camera_missile_view; 4 -> camera_eject_view. With no mechs at all it is forced to 2. Mode 0 is the only one in which camera_apply_zoom uses the player's zoom_factor (cameraZoomAlt is chosen when this is non-zero), and the only one that makes the player's own mech the camera subject. That is the shape of a cockpit view, but none of the modes is named by anything read here, so they stay numbers. PARTLY RESOLVED: 3 is the MISSILE CAMERA (camera_missile_view), 4 the EJECTION CAMERA (camera_eject_view) and 1 the external ORBIT camera (camera_orbit_update), each from its selector and its body. 2 is the FREE-FLYING camera (camera_free_fly), selected by the 'tinkerbell' cheat. CONVENTION, for a port: camera_update scales every camera control as value * tickDelta / 0xb6, so the control values are RATES PER SECOND; the eyepoint tilt keys give +/-0x2d0000 per second, 45 degrees a second with 0x1680000 as the full turn

cockpitViewActive.doc: 1 while the camera is in the player's own view this frame. camera_update clears it at the start of every frame (0x391ba) and camera_cockpit_view - the handler camera_update dispatches for cameraMode 0 and 6 - sets it (0x39b77); those are its only writers. cockpit_status_sounds plays the missile-lock tones only while it is set, and mech_damage_slot passes it as sound_play_at's last argument, where effect_spawn passes its own 'cameraMode is 0' test - so that argument is 'the listener is in the cockpit' by both callers' account, and it is sound_play_at's halveVolume, which sound_play_positional acts on by halving the volume (CORRECTION: this note said what sound_play_at does with it had not been read). mech_std_tick_ai also passes its inverse for one sound of the player's own mech. 16 more sites read it

ejectCameraMode.doc: the camera mode the view is LOCKED to once the player has ejected. -1 in the data; camera_set_mode, camera_init, camera_update (no-mechs branch) and camera_missile_view all test playerOut (formerly playerEjectedDone) and then substitute this for whatever mode they were about to use, storing 1 (camera_orbit_update) first if it is still -1. Nothing else writes it - those four are its only references (11 absolute-address uses, all inside them) - so in practice an ejected player always gets the orbit camera and cannot change it

cameraSubject.doc: the MechEntity the camera is attached to (typed MechEntity * because camera_track_cycle (formerly geom_luma_sub_039560) assigns mechTable[i] to it, and every reader dereferences mech offsets). camera_update sets it to the player's mech in cameraMode 0 when nothing else is set, and clears it when there are no mechs; a null subject forces mode 2

cameraTrackIndex.doc: the mechTable index camera_track_cycle steps with TRACK_NEXT / TRACK_PREV and wraps over mechCount; cameraSubject is set from it. command_execute (formerly option_toggle)'s external-view key and camera_init reset it to playerMechIndex (camera_init's note calls this "records the player's mech in 0x96f00" - it is the index, not a pointer)

playerEyeOffsetY.doc: int *, pointing at MechLoadout.eyeOffsetY of the loadout hud_widgets_install set up the cockpit for; null until then. Read by the cockpit camera and by weapon_build_fire_ray. QUIRK: weapon_build_fire_ray is used for EVERY mech's fire ray, so AI mechs get the player's eye offset added, not their own. It is harmless only because every MGEO record has 0 there

playerTorsoPanPtr.doc: int *, set by hud_widgets_install in the same breath as playerEyeOffsetY to &loadout->ramps[0].current, the torso pan ramp's current value. No reader was found in the exported source; it is labelled so the pair is visible, not because its use is known

ejectCamVelocity.doc: camera_eject_view's vertical speed, 16.16 cm per tick; 0 on entry

ejectCamAccel.doc: camera_eject_view's upward acceleration: 15520 in the image and never written. gravity's 0x794 = 1940 is one g in the same 16.16 cm-per-tick-squared units, and 15520 = 8 x 1940 exactly, so the ejection view climbs at 8 g

ejectCamStartTick.doc: simTick when camera_eject_view was entered; the spin rate grows with simTick - this

mainViewer.doc: the static Viewer record (0xbc bytes) that viewerPosition points at in the image (the dword at 0x9701c is 0x96f3c). The LITE chunk writes its lightPos and lightDirectional here by absolute address, 0x96f58..0x96f64, while it writes ambientLight through viewerPosition - the same record while the main view is current. Typed as a Viewer so those absolute writes print as fields: LITE's lightPos, VIEW's nearClip and farClip, and VWST's run from +0 to +0x18

viewerPosition.doc: the camera the renderer is currently drawing from. viewer_latch_globals latches it, and everything that needs a position relative to the eye reads it - the sound code subtracts posX, posY and posZ from a mech's own position to place a cue. Typing it as Viewer * rather than just labelling it is what turns its 206 accesses from raw pointer arithmetic into field reads.

shadedFillEnabled.doc: chooses the per-vertex-shade polygon filler 0x59e77 over flat filling. All three readers use it that way: map_fill_polygon calls 0x59e77 when set and the flat filler 0x59180 otherwise; render_asm_sub_03bb80 does the same; render_sky_and_ground draws its horizon band, whose vertices carry different shades, only when it is set. 1 in the image, and every write found sets 1 (four in damage.c's HUD/detail code). Presumably a detail option that something clears, but no clearing write was found

skyEnabled.doc: draws the region above the horizon. Which side it is comes from the extreme cases of render_sky_and_ground: with all four viewport corners above the horizon only this flag fires and it fills the whole rect, and with none above only groundEnabled does.
