Set per mission from record[0x11] == 0; damage clears it and groundEnabled together for a sequence that fills the viewport itself

groundEnabled.doc: draws the region below the horizon - see skyEnabled for how the two were told apart

horizonBandEnabled.doc: PLNT chunk [19] == 0, stored by project_chunk_exec at 0x4e6ba; initial 1. Its seven reads are all in render_sky_and_ground, where it gates building the horizon band - see horizonBandHeight. 45 of the 46 PLNT chunks leave [19] at 0, so the band is on almost everywhere

wireframeMode.doc: 0 normal drawing; non-zero replaces every polygon's colour with a false-colour index (polygon_resolve_colour, chosen by wireframeColourScheme) and the draw-list flush at 0x3cd64 ORs 0x2000 onto it, the outline mode. 1 first fills the polygon with colour 0 and then outlines it - hidden-line; 2 outlines only, so geometry behind shows through. Writers: the cheat that posts 'X-Ray vision enabled' sets 2; control 0x9e toggles 1, and only when the player mech's flag 0x2000 is set (what that flag is was not traced); the option callbacks read and write 1 for the same control; a damage.c view sequence sets 1 when 0x96840 is 1; debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section)'s command 0x8c (TOGGLE_WIREFRAME) cycles 0 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0. While it is non-zero vfx_video also skips render_sky_and_ground

wireframeColourScheme.doc: which false colours wireframeMode uses: 0 by object class and mech damage, 1 by WorldObject.objectClass, 2 by the flags' load bits (& 0x10f) - the tables are on polygon_resolve_colour. debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section)'s command 0x7b (COLLISION_WIREFRAME) cycles 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0; the cheat, control 0x9e and the damage.c sequence reset it to 0 when they turn wireframe on; the option callback ui_callbacks_sub_019b20 and the key cycle in debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section) (case 0x82) change wireframeMode without touching it

polygonRampOverride.doc: 0 in the image and NO WRITER: the only three references (0x12542, 0x38d0a, 0x38ea8) read it. When non-zero, polygon_resolve_colour would put every flat polygon on ramp 15 (0xf0) and the map hook 0x12520 would do the same. Dead in the shipped game

lightDimDistance.doc: LITE chunk +0x20. light_shade_level subtracts one shade level per this much of its distance argument when it is non-zero. 13000 to 100000 in the 46 LITE chunks, which would be 130 m to 1 km if the distance is in cm; that unit is not established. The LITE handler also sets 0x9705c to 1 when this is positive, and nothing in the code reads 0x9705c: a linear sweep of the code object finds only that store and effect_spawn's save, clear and restore

textureAffine.doc: non-zero skips the per-vertex rescale of a 0x5000 textured polygon's +0xc/+0x10 by focalScale / +0x14 in render_asm_sub_03bb80 - the divide a perspective-correct texture mapper needs, so non-zero is affine texturing. Mode 0x6000 forces it to 1 for its own draw. 0 in the image; the detail options set it through texture_perspective_set, the HUD inset views set 1. The reading of +0x14 as depth rests on the focalScale factor, not on a traced writer

textureOffTypeMask.doc: WorldObject.type bits whose textured polygons are drawn flat: polygon_resolve_colour turns modes 0x3000 and 0x5000..0x7000 into lit flat 0x1000 when (type & mask) is non-zero, and with bit 0x100 also for destructibles (family 0x50). 0 in the image. The detail options drive 0x100 and 0x200 together (mechs and gamethings) and 0x800 separately, through texture_type_set_enabled; debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section)'s commands 0x74, 0x75, 0x76 and 0x77 - TOGGLE_GP_TEXT_MAPS, TOGGLE_GT_TEXT_MAPS, TOGGLE_GS_TEXT_MAPS and TOGGLE_TERRAIN_TEXT_MAPS in commandNames - pass 0x100, 0x200, 0x400 and 0x800 (jump table 0x46c78, entries landing on 0x472db, 0x472ee, 0x47301, 0x47314). CORRECTION: this said the debug keys toggle only 0x200, 0x400 and 0x800 - the decompiled switch shows three cases and misplaces them; the jump table has four. The HUD inset views in hud_widget02_tick and damage_sub_030d30 set 0xb00 inside a save/restore of the 0x97020 block - flat mechs, gamethings and 0x800 objects in the small views

objectCullHook.doc: a function pointer: render_object_list and the scene-node pass call it for every object and draw the object only when it returns 0. The frame render in vfx_video uses object_cull_main_view by default, swaps in 0x3f780 for a pass with the far clip lifted and 0x3f970 for a pass with the near clip at 8, and restores the default after each. ortho_view_begin installs object_view_cull for its orthographic view. CORRECTION: this label first said vfx_font installs object_view_cull as the normal hook and vfx_video swaps in others for other modes, which had it the wrong way round

clipProjectHook.doc: a function pointer: poly_clip_and_queue calls it with every ClipVertex it makes (after clip_vertex_from_mesh and clip_vertex_at_near_plane) to fill screenX/screenY and the screen outcode. vfx_video_sub_010320 installs clip_project_perspective (0x3dfb7) beside objectCullHook and polygonDrawHook; ortho_view_begin installs 0x12ff0 for the overhead map's orthographic view

polygonDrawHook.doc: the polygon rasteriser the clipper calls for a normal polygon, sitting one slot below polygonFillHook and swapped the same way - vfx_video points it at 0x38ae0 in one place and 0x12520 in another. poly_clip_and_queue calls it as (polygon, vertexBase, firstVertex, polygonField0, extra), so the FOURTH argument is the polygon record's first 16-bit field, which arrives in ECX. WHAT THAT TELLS US ABOUT FIELD +0: the routine at 0x38ae0 masks it with 0x7000 straight away, so it is a BITFIELD with at least a three-bit selector in bits 12..14, not a plain index. The rest of its bits are not established. A PREVIOUS PASS FLAGGED A CONTRADICTION HERE and there is none: 0x38ae0 also dereferences the polygon's +0x20 as a pointer, which was noted as not fitting a 0x24-byte record. It fits - +0x20 is that record's last dword. What it points at is still unknown, and the OTHER implementation of this hook, at 0x12520, never reads it, working from the table at 0xa4c30 instead, so the field is not something every rasteriser needs. RESOLVED since: +0x20 is the owning WorldObject, the back-pointer mesh_add_polygon stores, and 0x38ae0 is now polygon_resolve_colour, which reads that object's type, flags and objectClass. The call is (poly, vertices, EBX unused, code, depth) - EBX is overwritten before it is read, and the stack argument, called extra above, is the polygon's view depth. The code's bits are laid out on polygon_resolve_colour

polygonFillHook.doc: the flat-colour polygon rasteriser, called as (count, vertices, colour). Swappable: vfx_video points it at render_asm_sub_03bb80 in one place and at 0x12690 in another. fill_triangle, fill_quad and fill_pentagon are fixed-arity wrappers that differ only in the count they pass - 3, 4 and 5 - which is what establishes the first argument as a vertex count rather than a mode.

horizonBandHeight.doc: HRZM ('horizon_map') chunk +0xc; default 36. The height of the gradient band render_sky_and_ground draws above the horizon line, shading the palette index from skyColour at its top to groundColour - 1 on the line. Only while horizonBandEnabled and 0x97024 are set. UNITS: pixels of a 320x200 design screen. main calls vfx_font_sub_014950 straight after sim_load_by_name, and that rescales this value in place with the same /319-then-canvas-scale pair it applies to the viewport rects. It passes the value as the X component, so the band grows with screen WIDTH, not height. render_sky_and_ground multiplies it by cos(roll). 60 to 200 across the 34 HRZM chunks in MW2.PRJ, 100 in most; planets with no HRZM keep 36

drawListCount.doc: entries appended to drawListCurrent this frame; reset to 0 at each walk

polysDrawn.doc: polygons appended this frame that kept more than one clipped vertex (the clipper counts only those); compared with polysDrawnLimit to stop the object walk

polysDrawnLimit.doc: the per-frame polygon budget: vfx_video_sub_010320 sets 0x578 (1400) after render_buffers_init. Once polysDrawn reaches it the object walks stop, so objects past the budget are not drawn that frame

currentViewportMode.doc: the viewportModes index currently selected. viewport_select is the only function that touches it, reading it to skip a redundant switch and writing it once the switch is done.

paletteCurrentSlot.doc: the slot currently on screen; palette_fade_step assigns paletteFadeTarget into it when a fade completes

paletteRestorePending.doc: set by palette_fade_step when a fade ends with no return leg; palette_apply_pending clears it and re-uploads paletteRestoreSlot, so the DAC is left holding a real palette rather than the fades last interpolated step

paletteBaseSlot.doc: the slot effect palettes are numbered relative to - palette_fade_for_effect adds EffectType.screenFadePalette to it. palette_fade_to_new_base is what sets it, and the disassembly at 0x3eaee shows the stored register is a copy of that functions slot argument, not the register noise the decompiler prints

paletteRestoreSlot.doc: the slot palette_apply_pending re-uploads. Set beside paletteBaseSlot by palette_fade_to_new_base, and defaulted to 0x10 during startup

paletteFadeTarget.doc: the slot palette_start_fade is fading towards

paletteFadeReturnTo.doc: the slot the fade started from, or -1; palette_fade_step fades back to it when paletteFadeReturnSteps is set

paletteFadeReturnSteps.doc: non-zero means run a return leg of this many steps when the fade ends, instead of just finishing

paletteFadeStepsLeft.doc: frames remaining in the running fade; 0 means no fade

paletteCycleActive.doc: palette_fade_step runs palette_cycle_step on paletteCycleState while it is set. Nothing writes it: colour cycling is dead in the shipped game

lodQuality.doc: the level-of-detail setting: 1 HIGH, 2 LOW - the game's own messages, 'LOD Quality HIGH' and 'LOD Quality LOW', posted by the keyboard toggle in debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section) (case 0x7b), which flips between exactly these two values. lod_quality_set and lod_quality_is_high are the options menu's setter and getter. viewer_update_projection forces it to at least 1 and divides Viewer.lodScale by lodQuality * 160, so LOW halves the distances at which objects switch to coarser meshes

cameraKeyCount.doc: how many cameraKeys are queued. camera_key_add appends at this index and refuses at 10; camera_keys_clear zeroes it; camera_keys_update and camera_key_begin stop at it

cameraKeysActive.doc: non-zero while the sequence plays. camera_keys_start sets it when at least one keyframe is queued; camera_keys_active returns it, and view_shake_impulse ignores a new impact while it is set, so shakes do not stack

soundRateTable.doc: ten playback rates in Hz: 9922, 10143, 10364, 10584, 10804, 11025, 11246, 11466, 11686, 11907. sound_channel_start uses entry 5 (0x970e4), 11025, for every one-shot; sound_emitter_update picks one at random (random_range(10)) on each volume update of a looping ambient emitter, so those wander in pitch between -10 and +8 percent

soundMixer.doc: the mixer block sound_init mallocs; 0 without a DIG driver, which every sound path tests

engineChannel.doc: signed byte: the MIDI channel engine_note_start locked for the player's engine note, -1 when none. engine_note_update and engine_note_mute act only while it is >= 0; engine_note_stop releases it and sets -1

midiDriver.doc: the Miles MIDI driver handle, opened by midi_open; 0 without a MIDI device, which silences the music and the engine note

midiReady.doc: 1 once midi_open has succeeded, cleared by midi_close; engine_note_start requires it

sflxScratch.doc: the SFLX decoder's 0x401-byte scratch buffer: each block is decoded (and upsampled) here and then copied out. It is never cleared between blocks or sounds, which is what makes method 1 (repeat) work, and why the upsamplers' read one past the stored samples picks up the previous block's data

radioAddressees.doc: three 12-byte {cueId, char *text, flags} records - 'All points', 'Point 2', 'Point 3' - indexed by MechEntity.starSlot and used as the prefix half of a radio line, so slot 1 reporting in comes out as 'Point 2 attacking your target'. The record layout is read straight out of sound_seq_queue_message, which takes field 0 as an int, field 1 as the char * it concatenates, and field 2 as an int. Only three records exist before lanceRadioMessages begins, which is the whole addressee vocabulary: a star has five slots and the table names two of them.

lanceRadioMessages.doc: the 11 lines a lancemate can say, in the same 12-byte records as radioAddressees: 0 'cannot do this', 1 'attacking your target', 2 'joining formation', 3 'patrolling your target', 4 'running awayyyyyy', 5 'reports target destroyed', 6 'destroyed', 7 'critical hit', 8 'ejecting', 9 'reports system shutdown', 10 'reports task complete. Rejoining formation'. The count is not guessed from where the strings stop - radio_lance_message guards its index with < 0xb, and index 10 is the last line before the formation announcements.

soundCueVariants.doc: three 12-byte records sitting immediately before soundCues, selected by sound_cue_play's second argument when it is positive. See the correction on soundCues: this is a window into one array that starts at 0x97950, not a table of its own.

soundCues.doc: 12-byte cue records - id, string pointer, flag - indexed by the first argument of sound_cue_play. CORRECTION to the shape this and soundCueVariants implied: they are not two tables. One contiguous array of 12-byte records starts at 0x97950 and runs past 0x97c08, and each player hands sound_seq_queue_message a different base inside it - radioAddressees at 0x97950, lanceRadioMessages at 0x97974, the formation lines at 0x979f8, soundCueVariants at 0x97a4c, soundCues here at 0x97a70. Every one of those addresses is 0x97950 plus a whole multiple of 12. The labels are still the right ones to read the call sites by; what was wrong was treating them as separate objects.

damageCallouts.doc: the voice callouts damage_callout_play plays, 0x28 entries of 12 bytes: +0 a sound id, +4 a pointer to the message text, +8 zero. The names below are read through those POINTERS, not by scanning the string area. 0 weapon destroyed, 1 internal ammo explosion detected, 2 NARC missle probe (sic), 3 anti-missle suite, 4 jump-jet exhaust port, 5 heat-sink, 6 life-support, 7 engine, 8 gyro, 9 sensors, 10 leg, 11 hip, 12 arm, 13 torso, 14..21 left leg, right leg, left arm, right arm, left torso, right torso, center torso, head, 22..35 the weapon families from LRM to small pulse laser, 36 autopilot, 37 ECM suite, 38 MASC; entry 39 is all zero. Every caller is mech_damage_slot, which is what turns this into the equipment-code table recorded there

voiceQueueHead.doc: the voice line playing (or posted) now, head of a list in descending priority; voice_queue_advance moves it on

voiceSample.doc: the HSAMPLE of the voice line playing, 0 when none: voice_line_start sets it and passes its address as the channel's user-data 0, so sound_sample_eos zeroes it when the line (with any chained body) ends

voiceQueueClosed.doc: set by voice_queue_close once the mission is decided; sound_seq_queue_message then queues nothing more

cdAudioReady.doc: every CD routine read so far (cd_audio_status, the play routine at 0x42f70, music_start_mission_track through cd_audio_ready) does nothing when this is 0. Its writer was not read

musicCdTrack.doc: the CD audio track the mission plays, the first number of the MUS resource; -1 for none (the image default) or after the play failed. It is the Redbook track number itself: cd_track_in_range checks it against the disc's cdTrackFirst..cdTrackLast, and the play routine indexes the per-track table at 0x15035c by (track - cdTrackFirst). FOR A PORT: mission music = CD track N, where N comes from MUSI -> MUS 'TRACKN'. The second number, into 0x97dfc, is 0 in every MUS resource. sound_seq_sub_043720 starts it through sound_seq_sub_0411c0 under bit 4 of 0x97e10 instead of bit 8. What it selects is not established

soundConfig.doc: the first of the 15 dwords main copies from mw2snd.cfg (or, when the file is missing, into a new one); read and written by the options menu handlers 0x43720..0x43b10, whose purpose was not read

sfxVolumeScale.doc: 16.16 scale on every effect's volume (sound_play, sound_play_delayed, the emitters); 1.0 in the image, cfg dword 1

voiceVolumeScale.doc: 16.16 scale on the voice lines' volume (voice_line_start, voice_resume); cfg dword 2

cdVolumeScale.doc: 16.16; cd_audio_init sets the CD volume to it * 255; cfg dword 3

soundFlags.doc: cfg dword 4 (0xb in the image, 0xf in a shipped MW2SND.CFG): 2 speech - clear, voice_line_start posts the line's text instead; 4 XMIDI music; 8 CD music

soundConfigBuffer.doc: the 0x3c-byte mw2snd.cfg image res_load_named_config returned; sound_save_config writes it back and frees it

soundPaused.doc: 1 between sound_pause and sound_resume (formerly sound_config_sub_043f70 / _043fd0); music_update restarts no track while it is set

musicTrackLoaded.doc: latch: music_start_mission_track parses the MUS resource only while this is 0, and sets it on the first call

soundSettingsInit.doc: 144 static records of four shorts {id, priority, maxPlaying, rate} that sound_settings_init copies into soundSettings by id. In the shipped image every rate is -1 (use the default, 11025 Hz); priority is 80 for 135 of them (the default when a sound has no record is 0x32 = 50); maxPlaying is -1 (unlimited) except 16 sounds limited to 1, 2 or 4 copies. tools/dump_sounds.py lists them per sound

netGameEnabled.doc: non-zero when the game was started as a network game. Set to 1 by check_launched_by_shell, out of the switch that parses the command line, and nothing else ever writes it. netplay_init does its entire body - buffer allocation, netRole (formerly aiLogEnabled) = 2 - inside a test on this, so without it netplay never starts. The cheat console is skipped while it is set, and the mech constructor uses it to choose between MechEntity.controlSource 1 and 2 for every non-player mech.

netActiveStations.doc: stations still in the game, this one included: the station count after the join, one less for each SS received. The send loop stops once this many (counting itself) have the packet; netplay_elect_master ends the session at 1

netStationCount.doc: short: the number of stations, net_station_info's low byte

netStatePacket.doc: the 72-byte (netStatePacketSize) DA buffer: netplay_build_state fills it from the player's mech, netplay_apply_state copies each received DA into it before applying it. Layout in netplay_build_state

netThingPacket.doc: the 35-byte (netThingPacketSize) SN buffer: 'SN' and the destroyed-gamething bitmap - see netplay_apply_thing_bitmap

netSessionState.doc: 0 no session (or the join failed), 1 running - netplay_frame_exchange does nothing otherwise - 2 signed off or last station standing

netRole.doc: this machine's role in a network game: 0 STANDALONE, 1 the network MASTER, 2 a network CLIENT. CORRECTION: this was labelled aiLogEnabled, 'gates the AI log lines', from a partial reading. Its writers are all in netplay: the network setup sets 2 when netGameEnabled; the station negotiation sets 1 when this machine's station id is the lowest active one (0x152980 == 0x152982) with simClockMode 0, and 2 otherwise with simClockMode 2; and it falls back to 0 when the network start fails. READERS: the outgoing state packet stamps simTick when it is 1, and the incoming one adopts the packet's simTick when it is 2, so the master owns the clock. The sim applies damage, heat and projectile hits to a mech only when this is 0 or the mech is playerMechIndex: in a network game each machine is authoritative for its own mech and learns the rest from packets. netplay_start (formerly netplay_sub_0446d0), run from main, starts the network session only when it is non-zero. The AI-log reading came from call sites that log only in single player or for the player's mech; anything annotated with the old name should be read as this

netNextSendTick.doc: simTick of the next state packet; netplay_frame_exchange sends when simTick reaches it and adds 0x12, so ten a second

shutdownOverrideRequest.doc: set to 1 by command_execute (formerly option_toggle)'s case 0x40 - the player asking to override a heat shutdown. The per-frame HUD dispatcher player_cockpit_frame (formerly sound_res_sub_032c50) consumes it every frame, clearing it either way: only when the player's loadout has flags bit 4 (shutdown pending) and not bit 8, and the display mode at 0xfe1a4 is not 3 (CORRECTION: 0xfe1a4 is playerStatusCopy, the player's MechLoadout.status, so: the mech is not already shut down), does it set bit 8, play sound 0xcd (MECBSOXX) and cue 2, 'Shutdown sequence overridden'. A request at any other time is simply lost. The options screen code at 0x19ab0/0x19b20 reads and restores it

alignLegsToTorso.doc: 1 while the player's legs are being turned to face where the torso points. CONFIRMED by name: the command that sets it, command_execute (formerly option_toggle) case 0x11, is FEET_TO_TORSO in the game's commandNames table. SET only by command_execute (formerly option_toggle) case 0x11; CLEARED only by mech_std_tick_ai when the job is done. mech_std_tick_ai, for the player while it is set: keeps the torso on its world bearing by taking each tick's heading change (heading - lastPlayerHeading, wrapped to +-180 degrees) off the twist, ramps[0], while driving the turn rate ramps[3] to +-0x370000 in the twist's direction; once the twist is within +-1 degree (0xffff) it zeroes ramps[0] and ramps[3], raises torso_pan_reset, zeroes control->torso_pan and clears this. Also while it is set: torso_pan is not copied into ramps[0].target, an engaged autopilot is switched off (as a legs-pan input does), and a stopped drive target of 0x400 is nudged to 0x480 so the mech creeps forward while it turns - the same nudge a legs-pan input gets

damageDisplayMode.doc: what the damage display in hudWidgets[2] shows; hud_widget02_tick switches on it. 0 nothing (the tick returns at once), 1 the section diagram (hud_damage_diagram_draw - the default arm, so any value above 5 would draw it too), 2 armour bars (damage_font_handler), 3, 4 and 5 a rendered view of the player's own mech through render_view_from_pose with different poses and effect_draw_cached_alt frames 0xfa / 0xf7 / 0xfd. Initialised to 1 in the data. damage_display_mode_cycle steps it 1..5; command_execute (formerly option_toggle) cases 3..7 set 2..5 or toggle 0/1 directly. THE COMMANDS, by the game's own names (commandNames; command_execute (formerly option_toggle) switches on the command id): 2 MFD_CYCLE steps the modes, 3 TOGGLE_HTAL toggles mode 2 (the armour bars - Head/Torso/Arm/Leg), 4 TOGGLE_REAR_VIEW mode 3 (its view is rendered from heading + 180 degrees), 5 TOGGLE_DOWN_VIEW mode 4, 6 TOGGLE_WEAPON_DISPLAY mode 5, and 7 TOGGLE_DAMAGE_DISPLAY toggles between 0 and 1 (the section diagram). So this is the multi-function display's mode; the name is kept because every reader already uses it, and what modes 4 and 5 draw beyond the command names was not checked

exitPromptShown.doc: set once 'Press any key to exit...' has been posted, by mission_results_update (formerly exit_prompt) more than 3 seconds after the player's group's mission result. key_command_update treats any key as a quit request while it is set

hangAround.doc: toggled by the cheat 'hangaround', which answers 'Now how do I win?' when it turns on and 'That's better' when it turns off. While set, mission_results_update skips the mission-end exit timing entirely: no 'Press any key to exit' and no automatic quit, so the player can stay in a finished mission. The cache also reads it, to choose between its debug and player-facing out-of-memory messages, so it doubles as a verbose flag

crackModeEnabled.doc: gates command 0x89 CRACK_MODE: command_execute toggles time compression only while this is set. Its only other writer is cheat_handle_command, which flips it for the cheat typed as 'lairdo' (listing/cheats.txt) and posts 'ATTENTION ENEMIES: Don't mess with...'; 0 in the data

netMessageTerminator.doc: the four bytes 'EOP\xff' net_queue_message writes after every message and net_next_message scans for

testDamageSlot.doc: the slot index for the testDamageLocation damage test: debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section) sets 0..9 from ten option commands; -1 means none pending, and mech_std_tick_ai resets it to -1 after applying the hit

testDamageLocation.doc: a hit location chosen from the keyboard: debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section) stores 1..8 here and posts the location's name - Head, Right Torso, Center Torso, Left Torso, Right Arm, Left Arm, Right Leg, Left Leg, in that order. mech_std_tick_ai then calls mech_damage_slot(player's loadout, testDamageLocation, testDamageSlot, 0) and resets testDamageSlot to -1, so the player's OWN mech takes a critical there. A developer damage-test feature; its value to a port is that it names all eight 1-based locations

pausePane.doc: the pane cheats_sub_046ac0 (PAUSE_GAME) draws SHP assetVariant + 0x5e in: {0, 0, 0.2, 1.0, 0.4} as fractions in the image; on first use it gets &defaultCanvas, becomes window pixels and is fitted to the shape (layout_pane_fit_shape), and the flip is given it

pausePaneStale.doc: 1 in the image: cheats_sub_046ac0 lays pausePane out on its first pause and clears it

commandNames.doc: 153 packed 5-byte records {char *name; byte id} - the game's names for its player commands. input_load_gamekeys walks them (0x48664: name at [i*5 + 0x9dca4], compared with stricmp; 0x48676: id at [i*5 + 0x9dca8]; cmp esi, 0x99) and stores the id of the matching name into the byte table at 0x9dfa1, indexed by key - a key binding map whose reader was not traced. The ids are the command numbers debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section) switches on (its jump table at 0x46c78 is indexed by id - 10), checked three ways: TOGGLE_WIREFRAME (0x8c) writes wireframeMode, TOGGLE_LOD_QUALITY (0x85) writes lodQuality, COLLISION_WIREFRAME (0x7b) cycles wireframeColourScheme. THE ID FOLLOWS ITS NAME: pairing each id with the pointer after it instead puts every name one command off, which is the mistake the first reading of this table made. strings.txt shows the name of command 0x74 as 'OTOGGLE_GP_TEXT_MAPS' at 0x92adf - a splice; the pointer here is 0x92ae0

debugPaletteToggle.doc: flipped by debug_command_execute for TOGGLE_PALETTE (0x8d); what it switches is not established here

debugShowFramerate.doc: developer display flag, flipped by debug_command_execute for TOGGLE_FRAMERATE (0x88) and for TOGGLE_FRAMERATE_MAIN (0x7c); 0 or 1

debugShowFramerateMain.doc: set to debugShowFramerate's new value by TOGGLE_FRAMERATE_MAIN (0x7c) only - the plain command leaves it alone. By the command name, the same display on the main screen as well; its readers were not traced

debugShowSceneInfo.doc: developer display flag, flipped by debug_command_execute for TOGGLE_SCENE_INFO (0x8b) and for TOGGLE_SCENE_INFO_MAIN (0x7e); 0 or 1

debugShowSceneInfoMain.doc: set to debugShowSceneInfo's new value by TOGGLE_SCENE_INFO_MAIN (0x7e) only - the plain command leaves it alone. By the command name, the same display on the main screen as well; its readers were not traced

debugShowEyePosition.doc: developer display flag, flipped by debug_command_execute for TOGGLE_EYE_POSITION (0x8a) and for TOGGLE_EYE_POSITION_MAIN (0x7f); 0 or 1

debugShowEyePositionMain.doc: set to debugShowEyePosition's new value by TOGGLE_EYE_POSITION_MAIN (0x7f) only - the plain command leaves it alone. By the command name, the same display on the main screen as well; its readers were not traced

debugShowMemInfo.doc: flipped by debug_command_execute for TOGGLE_MEM_INFO (0x79), which also copies it to debugShowMemInfoMain (0x9e8a0)

debugShowMemInfoMain.doc: the copy TOGGLE_MEM_INFO makes of debugShowMemInfo; readers not traced

randomRangeCursor.doc: random_range own cursor, kept in 0..126 by a mod 0x7f

randomNextCursor.doc: random_next own cursor. It indexes with cursor + 1 BEFORE the mod, so it reads entries 1..127 while randomRangeCursor reads 0..126 - different conventions, both in bounds, neither an off-by-one

mainProject.doc: the projectFiles record index of the open mw2.prj. project_open stores what project_file_open returns and fatal_errors on -1, and project_shutdown passes it to project_close. It is the first argument of nearly every cache_load_resource call - 67 references in the export. It is an INDEX, always 0, since project_file_open only ever uses record 0; the file handle is projectFiles +0. CORRECTION: the first version of this note called it the handle of the open file

projectOpenPath.doc: the path project_open opens. If it is still null at open it defaults to the string 'mw2.prj' after screenshot_sub_04c4b0 and clib_sub_062b86 have processed it. A command-line switch written as two characters, '=' and a path (case 8 of the argument switch in netplay.c) points it at the text after the '='. Which switch letters that is has not been established. RENAMED from projectFileName, a name that was already taken: projectFileName is the char[0x20] at +0x12a of each projectFiles record, where project_file_open keeps a copy of this path. The two labels existed side by side for one increment

projectAllocHook.doc: indirect allocator project_load_directories calls with a directory's byte size; paired with projectFreeHook, which it calls on a failed seek or short read. Swappable pointers rather than direct malloc/free calls, the same arrangement file_load uses

crashDepth.doc: how many times a crash routine has been entered. All three share it and switch on its old value, so a fault raised while tearing down after a fault skips the step that faulted and still reaches exit

looseFilesFirst.doc: set by the -P command-line option. project_open_stream (formerly project_lookup_id) then takes its loose-file branch for EVERY lookup - the one otherwise used only for ids that resolved to -1 or -2 - and when res_load_file fails it carries on instead of calling system_error. So files on disk stand in for the project container: a development override

projectTraceEnabled.doc: set by the -E command-line option, which also opens mw2debug.txt. project_open_stream (formerly project_lookup_id) then logs every lookup ('Prj file ID#%d' or the name) and project_walk_chunks every chunk tag, known or not (project_trace_chunk, formerly project_log_unknown_tag, which described it wrongly); those are its only readers

streamSeenHead.doc: first record of the seen-stream list, or null. Each record is 15 bytes from cache_alloc: next at +0, the short id at +4, 8 name characters at +6 and a NUL at +0xe. stream_seen_find walks from here; stream_seen_add sets it when the list is empty; stream_seen_clear frees the chain and zeroes it. The gate for dtblCountANTK and dtblBytesANFL. The game calls it the file ID list: stream_seen_add's allocation failure is system_error 0x42, SYSERR_CANTMALLOCFILEIDLIST

weaponRatingValues.doc: 31 shorts, one per weaponTypes index, read by mech_loadout_rating (mov dx, [eax*2 + 0x9eb2c] at 0x4d048) as each mounted weapon's contribution to loadoutRating: code / 100 indexes it. Values: LRM20 183, LRM15 137, LRM10 91, LRM5 46 (linear in tubes), SRM6 51, SSRM6 74, GAUSS 228, PPC 228, LLASER 166, LPLAS 177, uAC20 329, xAC20 157, MGun 2, FLAMER 4, AMS 40, NARC 50, NUKE 0

scenarioTable.doc: the table the STBL chunk supplies - scenario_table in the game's vocabulary - copied whole into a cache block by scenario_table_load. An 8-byte header then records of 0xc bytes, the stride coming from the count it derives as (size - 8) / 0xc. Only one of these exists, where missions get sixteen slots. THE RECORDS ARE NAMES: project_item_apply strncpys 0xc bytes straight out of scenarioTable + 8 + index * 0xc as a 12-character name, which both confirms the stride from a second direction and says what a record holds

scenarioTableIndex.doc: the read position in scenarioTable. RESOLVED - it was named from a single bounds check and flagged as having only one consumer behind the name. project_item_apply is the second: it takes the name at the current index and then increments it, so the scenario list is consumed in order as the project file loads. scenario_table_load clears it when a new table arrives

thingNodeCount.doc: entries appended to thingNodeQueue so far this mission, capped at 0x96

thingNodeNext.doc: thingNodeQueue's read position; thing_node_queue_pop returns null once it reaches thingNodeCount

projectIdMangle.doc: the namespace added to every object id a project chunk carries. RENAMED from geomBase, described as 'the base every loaded-geometry offset is measured from'. CORRECTION: nothing is measured from it. project_mangle_id adds it and the sum is only ever an equality key into the three id maps (projectObjectMap, the detail map, the world record map). project_set_mangle writes it: 0 from sim_load_by_name and MOFF, and projectMangleNext - whose high word MON bumps - from MON. So it is n << 16 for the n-th mangle_on region

projectMangleNext.doc: the next id namespace. Only the MON chunk touches it: it adds 1 to the high word and hands the whole dword to project_set_mangle, so namespaces run 0x10000, 0x20000, ...

formationOverridePlayer.doc: char *, null unless the command line carries -OF=name (or /OF=): check_launched_by_shell switches on toupper(argv[i][1]) - 'B', and its case 0xd, letter O, takes argv[i][2] - F here - and points this at argv[i] + 4, past the '='. star_table_load then uses it instead of the STAR chunk's formation name for playerGroupIndex's group. So a launcher can set the player's lance formation. Its only relocations are that store and star_table_load's read

formationOverrideEnemy.doc: char *, the -OE=name twin of formationOverridePlayer - letter E in the same case of check_launched_by_shell - which star_table_load uses for EVERY group other than the player's. Its only relocations are that store and star_table_load's read

currentGamepiece.doc: the mech the mission file is defining right now. project_chunk_exec's GP (gamepiece) case sets it to each mech it spawns, and to 0 when the gamepiece's object is not found. The chunks after it act on it: EYEO sets its aimNode, POFO fills its loadout's sectionNodes, MGDF loads its geometry parameters into the loadout, and HUDF loads a HUD file, but only when its controlSource is 0, the player. All four do nothing while it is 0. anim_player_step's INIT also binds a new animation task to it, and fails with animPlayerError when it is 0

projectEntryHandlers.doc: 6 slots, every target in the project_entry module

projectileSlotFill.doc: the next projectiles[] slot a BTHG chunk stocks. project_chunk_exec is its only user: it reads it, fills that slot if it is empty and the chunk's object has a node, and increments it either way, ignoring chunks once it reaches 0xaf. It is 0 in the image and NOTHING RESETS IT, from a scan of every function for the address. So the pool is stocked once per run of MW2.EXE; a second stocking would start at slot 159. See Projectile.id for the per-kind counts

xploSlotFill.doc: the next simSlots entry an XPLO chunk fills. Only the XPLO branch of project_chunk_exec touches it - two reads and the increment at 0x4f4c7 are its only relocations - and it refuses at 0x100, so XPLO chunks pre-build simSlots 0, 1, 2 ... in file order. 0 in the image and never reset

polyLoadStatus.doc: written on every exit path of poly_load_wtbo_record: -2 (0xfffffffe) for a bad magic, a failed allocation or a checksum mismatch, -9 (0xfffffff7) when a polygon cannot be added - the field is typed int, so the exported source shows the signed forms, and the checksum XOR - so zero - on success. poly_load_wtbo_block clears it on entry. NOTHING IN THE DECOMPILED SOURCE READS IT, so whether it is a real error channel or a debugging leftover is not established

wtboLowFlagIs2.doc: WRITE-ONLY, the partner of wtboLowFlagIs1: 1 when (WTBO flags & 0xcfff) == 2. All four references (0x4ff17, 0x4ffa8, 0x4ffc2, 0x4ffd2) are stores in poly_load_wtbo_record

wtboLowFlagIs1.doc: WRITE-ONLY. poly_load_wtbo_record sets it to 1 when (WTBO flags & 0xcfff) == 1, 0 otherwise; all four references (0x4ff1d, 0x4ffae, 0x4ffbd, 0x4ffcc) are stores in that function, and the whole image holds the address nowhere else. So the WTBO flags' low bits do nothing in the shipped game, although the data sets them: 2589 records have 1, 2819 have 2, 375 have 3 and 11 have 0

polyVertexOffsetX.doc: x of the translation added to every vertex of a POLY mesh as it is loaded. Set by poly_set_vertex_offset, which is the handler for the PLGO chunk - the game's own project vocabulary calls that tag polyoffset. poly_load_wtbo_record (formerly sim_objects_sub_04fef0) applies it as offset + coordinate x scale, per component

polyVertexOffsetY.doc: y of the POLY load translation - see polyVertexOffsetX

polyVertexOffsetZ.doc: z of the POLY load translation - see polyVertexOffsetX

polyVertexScaleX.doc: x of the per-component scale every POLY vertex is multiplied by as it is loaded, set by poly_set_vertex_scale. A zero argument is coerced to 1 by the setter, so the multiply can never collapse a mesh to a point

polyVertexScaleY.doc: y of the POLY load scale - see polyVertexScaleX

polyVertexScaleZ.doc: z of the POLY load scale - see polyVertexScaleX

polyLoadFlags.doc: the flag bits the next mesh load stamps onto its objects: set by poly_set_load_flags, read only by poly_load_wtbo_block, which passes it to object_apply_load_flags for every object it builds (bits 0x10f are used). Its meaning on the object is not established. IN THE DATA (tools/dump_objects.py, the OBJ chunk's +0x32 over all 12182 chunks): 0 on 11260, 1 on 206 (every one a clan-colour *SCR1 mesh, family 0x30), 2 on 321 (T*CST* meshes and TL1DMSTR), 4 on 391 (panel meshes - *SPNL*, *PANL*, *SPIV* - plus TNJ1SCR1 and the LAS0_* meshes), and 3 on four (TL1SHIEL, SAAINDPC, S_BINDPC, S_BINDPD); the 0x100 depth-sort bit is never set by an OBJ chunk. So bits 0-3 look like a per-mesh drawing mode, but no reader was found above the rasteriser: render_object_list tests only 0x100, and object_draw_lod_mesh hands polygons straight to poly_clip_and_queue. What 1, 2 and 4 select is NOT established. RESOLVED since: they are the polygon depth-sort mode - see WorldObject.flags and polySortFlags. The claim just above was wrong: render_object_list also LATCHES the whole flags word for the clipper, which is where 1, 2 and 4 are read

polyCodeRemapLimit.doc: the highest code polyCodeRemapTable may be indexed with. 0 in the image and never written - the same whole-image sweep finds only poly_resolve_code's two reads (0x4fe5b, 0x4fe7a)

wtboPartClass.doc: 4 in the image and never written - its one reference is the read at 0x50471. poly_load_wtbo_record passes it to object_set_class for each part after the first of a wtboPartMode block; objectClass 4 is the class object_set_class takes OFF the world chain, so those parts are drawn through their scene nodes, not the chain

projectKeywords.doc: 0x48 pointers to the source keywords MW2's .prj files were written in, parallel to projectTags. This is the whole vocabulary of the data format: planet, terrain, gp_chassis_table, navpoint, task, formation, affiliation, orders, goal_on/goal_off and so on.

projectTags.doc: 0x48 four-byte chunk tags, in the order the project-file reader searches them. Parallel to projectKeywords - project_tag_to_keyword indexes both with the same i - and the pairing is self-evident once printed: PLNT/planet, TERR/terrain, NAVP/navpoint. tools/dump_project_tags.py writes the full list to listing/project_tags.txt.

effectLightActive.doc: whether the mission's light (lightPos, lightDirectional, ambientLight, 0x9705c) has been saved to 0x1538f8..0x15390c and replaced by an effect. Set once when the first lighting effect takes over and cleared when it is handed back, so a second effect moves the light without re-saving. CORRECTION: named cameraOverridden, read as the viewer's aim point and angles; see lightPos.

lightEffectSlot.doc: which simSlots entry's effect is currently the scene light, or -1. Written by effect_spawn when an effect with lightsScene takes over, and put back to -1 by sim_slots_update when that slot expires; the slot's own SimSlot.ownsLight says the same thing from the other side. CORRECTION: named cameraEffectSlot while the light was misread as the camera.

playerLastMissile.doc: the projectiles[] slot of the player's most recent missile. mech_weapon_fire sets it to the slot it just launched when the round is projectile kind 3 or 4 (SRMs, NARC, LRMs, Streaks) and to -1 when the player launches any other kind. missile_cam_follow_last reads it

missileCamProjectile.doc: the projectiles[] slot the missile camera is following, or -1. Set by missile_cam_follow_last and refreshed by projectile_update while the slot's missileCam is set. Reset to -1 by projectile_destroy, by missile_cam_pose once the flag is gone, and by a failed follow

killCreditMech.doc: which mech is credited with the kill currently being resolved, or -1. projectile_update writes Projectile.attackerMechIndex here as the shot lands, and whichever death path runs next reads it: gamething_destroy for a world object, mech_apply_damage for a mech. Both bucket the kill by status into three counters and both do it twice - once when it equals playerMechIndex, once for the wider tally, which for a mech kill is the whole of the player's star rather than everyone. Both then put it back to -1.

effectMountMech.doc: RENAMED from effectMountNode, which was the wrong kind of thing: it holds a MechEntity *, not a node. Every caller of effect_spawn_on_mount passes loadout->entity, and effect_align_to_mount reads the node from it at +0x48, MechEntity.mountNode. where effect_spawn_on_mount leaves the object an effect should hang off, because effect_spawn takes no such argument. effect_spawn consults it only for effect indices from 0x17 up, and hands it to effect_align_to_mount to copy that object's node transform onto the effect's own node. Every weapon muzzle effect goes through this. ONE-SHOT, but only on the aligned path: effect_spawn clears it right after effect_align_to_mount (0x513a2 xor ebx, ebx; 0x513a9 stores ebx here, and effect_align_to_mount saves and restores ebx). The export showed that as effectMountMech = extraout_EBX until the cspec modelled register preservation; it now reads effectMountMech = (MechEntity *)0x0. When the effect index is below 0x17, or the claimed slot has no node (the branch at 0x51387), it is NOT cleared, so a mech left here would still be here for the next effect from 0x17 up. HARMLESS, checked: effect_spawn uses only the low byte of its index (and esi, 0xff at 0x5108b), and of its six callers only effect_spawn_on_mount can pass a low byte from 0x17 up - which it sets this global immediately before. The others pass 0x16 (nuke_detonate), the weapons' impact effects (low bytes 0..0x16, or 0xff which is refused as over 0x1f), 3 / 0xd / 0x0b (gamething_apply_damage, from 0x20b), 7 / 3 / 0xd / 0x0b (effect_spawn_at's three callers) and 0x0b (effect_spawn's own chained 0x10b). The index switch cannot lift one over the line either: it remaps 0..6 by flag bits to values no higher than 0x15, sends 0x0b to effect_spawn_fragments and returns, and passes the rest through. So a stale value is always overwritten before it could be read.

effectLightsAllowed.doc: CORRECTION: named effectCameraCutsAllowed while the scene light was misread as a camera override (see EffectType.lightsScene). effect_spawn only lets an effect become the scene light when its effectTypes[].lightsScene is set and this is non-zero. The PLNT handler sets it to ([16] == 0) - see gravity for the record - and 42 of the 46 PLNT records in MW2.PRJ have [16] = 1, so most worlds suppress the cut

nukeBlastTicksLeft.doc: how long the nuke blast keeps damaging, in ticks: twice effectTypes[0x16].lifetime (10920 ticks, 60 s) at detonation, - tickDelta per tick in nuke_blast_update, which does nothing once it reaches 0. It sits 4 bytes before weaponTypes

chainFireMode.doc: 1 in CHAIN FIRE, 0 in GROUP FIRE; 1 in the image. Its only references are in mech_weapons_tick: the toggle_group_fire control flips it, playing cue 6 'Chain fire' going to 1 and cue 7 'Group fire' going to 0 (read from soundCues), and while it is 0 the player's weapon_fire is moved onto weapon_fire_group, so the trigger arms the whole current group through player_fire_group instead of the one selected weapon. One global, not per mech; only the player's control path sets the channels it redirects

videoWaitHook.doc: a VFX driver hook that paces: palette_fade_used_colours calls it duration times over a fade, and main's display step calls it before the page flip when 0x95514 is set - consistent with a wait for vertical retrace, which is NOT established

paletteDacRead.doc: the VFX driver hook palette_fade_used_colours calls with (index, destination) for each colour it will fade: the hardware DAC entry read back into paletteWorking. Named for that use and for sitting beside paletteDacWrite in the driver table

paletteDacWrite.doc: indirect hook called once per palette entry after paletteDac is written - the DAC poke. game_boot shifts three consecutive bytes right by 2 before each call, which is 8-bit colour narrowed to the VGA DACs 6 bits and is what fixes this as the hardware palette path

paletteWorking.doc: 256 three-byte entries: palette_fade_used_colours reads each colour it will fade from the hardware DAC into here (the hook paletteDacRead, with the entry index and this entry's address), steps it toward the target and writes it back with paletteDacWrite. RESOLVED: the first note left its relation to paletteDac open; paletteDac is the palette last UPLOADED (palette_set_entries, before the brightness remap), this is a read-back of the hardware, so it carries the remap

paletteUsedIndices.doc: the distinct palette indices found on the canvas, in first-seen order; palette_fade_used_colours builds it and then walks it backwards

paletteFadeDelta.doc: per-channel distance from paletteWorking to the target, as a magnitude; the sign lives in paletteFadeScratch

paletteFadeScratch.doc: reused for two things by palette_fade_used_colours: first 256 bytes of seen-flags while it collects paletteUsedIndices, then per-channel step direction, +1 or -1, for the fade itself. The dual use is in the binary, not a mistake in the naming

paletteFadeAccum.doc: per-channel Bresenham accumulator, primed to half the largest delta so each channel takes its first step near the middle of its run

currentViewport.doc: a copy of the selected viewportModes record, five ints, refreshed by viewport_select. Several render and geometry routines read it rather than indexing the table themselves.

defaultCanvas.doc: a five-int record of the same shape as currentViewport and each viewportModes entry - render_asm_sub_03eb10 copies both with the same five-iteration loop. project_tables, damage and sound_res all store its address into draw-target slots, so it is the record everything points at by default, and palette_fade_used_colours scans its pixels. WHETHER IT IS LITERALLY THE VISIBLE FRAMEBUFFER IS NOT ESTABLISHED - default target is what the call sites show

screenModeInfo.doc: the display mode as the VFX driver reports it: vfx_load_drivers stores what the driver entry at [0x9fd48] returns. [0] is the width and [1] the height - screen_select_asset_variant matches them against 320x200 / 640x480 / 1024x768 in that order, and video_init allocates [0] * [1] bytes as the framebuffer. Nothing past [1] has been read

frameProjTable.doc: 96 records of 8 bytes that FPRJ (frame_prj) chunks append through frame_prj_add: dword at +0 from chunk +0xc as a ushort (the chunk is skipped when it is 0xffff), short at +4 from chunk +8 (-1 becomes 1), short at +6 from chunk +0xa (-1 becomes 0). WRITE-ONLY: every relocation into 0xa4710..0xa4a0f is in frame_prj_add, frame_prj_slot_clear or the unreached frame_prj_reset, and no FPRJ chunk occurs in MW2.PRJ. The fields are therefore left unnamed - there is no consumer to name them from, and a port can parse and drop the chunk

anim2dSlots.doc: the Anim2D records ANM2 chunks add, 7 at most: anim2d_add refuses at anim2dCount >= 7. anim2d_draw, anim2d_free and anim2d_rewind index it by slot. project_chunk_exec discards anim2d_add's return, so the first ANM2 lands in slot 0 - the slot hud_widget02_tick and hud_widget13_tick draw

messageText.doc: the two message slots' 0x100-byte text buffers

screenAspect.doc: height / width * 4/3 in 16.16 - 0xd555 (0.833) at 320x200, 0x10000 at 640x480 and 1024x768. viewer_set_aspect_from_screen stores it here and in viewerPosition->aspectScale. WRITE-ONLY: that store is the only relocation that targets it

assetVariant.doc: which resolution's 2D art to load: 0 = 320x200 (the plain SHP/FONT name), 1 = 640x480 (name + '6'), 2 = 1024x768 (name + 'K'). Every reader adds it to an SHP or FONT resource id - a base id whose next two directory slots are the '6' and 'K' versions, true of all 91 SHP triplets and the FONT one in MW2.PRJ. Written only by screen_select_asset_variant (the one store, mov [0xa4dc0], bl at 0x1492d); 0 in the image, so 320x200 art when no mode matches

brightnessTables.doc: 16 tables of 64 bytes (6-bit colour in, 6-bit out) built by brightness_tables_build; palette_apply_brightness maps the palette through one

paletteDac.doc: 256 entries of three bytes, the palette last uploaded: palette_set_entries writes the caller's colours here and pokes paletteDacWrite per entry with the colour mapped through brightnessTables[brightnessShown] - so the hardware holds the remapped colours and this the unmapped ones, which palette_apply_brightness remaps again. CHANNEL ORDER IS NOT ESTABLISHED, so the +1 and +2 bytes keep their bare labels rather than being called green and blue

dayPhaseStart.doc: int[4], seconds: dayLengthSeconds/24 * 5, 7, 17, 19, set by day_cycle_init. day_cycle_tick picks the last one not above timeOfDay

dayCycleNextTick.doc: simTick at which day_cycle_tick next re-evaluates; it adds 0x71c (10 s)

dayCycleWarmup.doc: day_cycle_tick's first two calls only count this up; at 2, day_cycle_set_phase makes a 2 s fade and sets it to 3

dayCycleEnabled.doc: byte. day_cycle_set_phase does nothing unless it is 1. Cleared while the 0xa55e9 overlay mode holds palette slot 0xc, set again when that mode ends. 0xa55e9, the byte after it, is LEFT UNNAMED: command 0x9d toggles it (cheat_handle_command and ui_callbacks) through vfx_font_sub_0150f0, which refuses unless hudWidgets[0] +6 < 1, fades to slot 0xc and plays sound 0xb2 and cue 0x1c. An unreferenced string 'Light amplification' sits at 0x91486, but no xref ties it to this, so light amplification is a guess

infraredOn.doc: byte: whether the INFRARED vision mode is on. command_execute case 0x9d, INFRARED, asks vfx_font_sub_0150f0 to set it to the inverse of its current value; day_cycle_tick and day_cycle_set_phase test it - the day-cycle notes call it the 0xa55e9 overlay mode

launchAnimNameG.doc: char *, the -G=name command-line option: the same for the SECOND launch file, whose default stem is 'launch'

launchAnimNameB.doc: char *, the -B=name command-line option: boot_load_launch_anims builds the FIRST launch file it loads as <drive>launch\<this><variant suffix>, with 'supanm' when this is null or empty

missionEndCode.doc: 1 at startup, 2 when the player ejected and 4 when the player was refused an ejection and died instead. RESOLVED: an earlier pass recorded 2-versus-4 as unestablished and named it only by position. The separator is ejectDisabled. With it clear, mech_eject leaves status at 5 (ej) and the tick writes 2; with it set, the tick rewrites status to 4 (dd) and writes 4 here. It is READ EXACTLY ONCE, as (code & 4), by palette_fade_screen_to_preset at the end of main's mission loop, so palette slot 0x10 covers both completing and ejecting and slot 0x11 is specifically the refused-ejection death. Nothing distinguishes 1 from 2 - only bit 2 ever matters.

missionMusicResource.doc: MUSI ('music') chunk +8 as a short, or resource_id_by_name(0xc, chunk + 10) when that is -1. Type 0xc is MUS. Read only by music_start_mission_track. The 45 MUSI chunks in MW2.PRJ name track2..track26, and their ids agree with the names

missionMusicName.doc: the MUSI chunk's name string ('track10'), copied from +10. WRITE-ONLY: the copy at 0x4e7b8 is the only reference in the image

objectiveTables.doc: TYPED as ObjectiveTable[16] by applyObjectiveTables; 16 x 0x2e8a ends exactly at groupCurrentObjective (0xd3ff0). The runtime objective tables, one per group, 0x2e8a bytes apart, missionTableCount of them. HEADER, from objective_table_install, which fills it from the MTBL chunk (chunk offsets in brackets), and from its readers. +0 objective count: (chunk size - 0x26) / 0x97. +4 start time in missionSeconds: -1 at install, stamped by objective_table_start. +8 decision time: -1 at install, stamped by mission_results_update when the result is decided. +0xc time limit in seconds [+0xc]: mission_results_update gives result 4 once missionSeconds - (+4) reaches it, and 0 or less means no limit. +0x10 a SNDS id [the name at +0x12, resolved through SNDTABLE, i.e. resource_id_by_name(0xb)]. +0x38 objectiveTableResult. +0x39 the group's affiliation, from groupTable. +0x3a the objective records, 0xf7 bytes each: see missionRecordState, which is +0x3a of table 0. Objective 0 must be type 0x10, the start objective; objective_table_install fatal_errors otherwise, and objective_table_start takes the group's start position from its first target

objectiveTableResult.doc: a byte at +0x38 of each 0x2e8a-byte objective table, i.e. 0xa5750 + table * 0x2e8a + 0x38: the table's overall MISSION result. mission_result_text shows 'Mission successful' and plays the table's S resource at 2, 'Mission failed' and the F resource at 3, and 'Mission time exceeded' with the fixed resource BET68 at 4, but only for the player's group. objective_evaluate writes 2 for an objective of type 0x10000 and 3 for 0x20000, so the mission ends through an objective like any other. objective_debug_view (formerly mission_log_star) confirms the values independently, for every star, not just the player's: 0 'Star %d mission: in progress' (or '%d sec left'), 2 'Successful at', 3 'Failed at %d sec', 4 'Out of time at' - which also fixes that each objective table belongs to one star, i.e. one group. mission_save_results (formerly mission_load_config) reads it too

missionRecordState.doc: RENDERING CAVEAT: since the table was typed, this label sits inside an array, and readers that form the address as a plain integer (base + index * stride) now print the raw hex 0xa578a instead of this name - the decompiler neither resolves it to a field path nor falls back to the label in integer arithmetic. Before typing they printed (int)&missionRecordState + ... ; the typed readers gained field names, these lost the label. TYPED: this is objectiveTables[0].objectives[0], an Objective; the struct field notes are the current word and this note is the history. RESOLVED below: the 58-byte gap is the ObjectiveTable header, 0x3a + 48 x 0xf7 = 0x2e8a exactly. The runtime half of a mission record - the table itself holds 0x97 bytes of static data, this holds 0xf7 bytes of state, and the two are indexed alike. Layout as its two readers use it: a state byte at +0 taking 0, 1 or 7, (7 is OPEN FOR TARGETS - set by mission_mark_by_name while the stream of the same name runs, and the only state mission_record_add_value will attach a target to; see mission_mark_by_name), a flags dword at +2 tested against a caller mask, a count byte at +0xd6 capped at 16, and that many ushorts from +0xd7. The stride is self-confirming - 0xd7 plus sixteen 2-byte entries is exactly 0xf7. Records run 48 to a table and tables are 0x2e8a apart, which is 58 bytes MORE than 48 x 0xf7; whether that gap is padding or a per-table header has not been chased. These are the mission records the MTBL chunk supplies - see missionTables - but the meaning of the state values, the flags and the appended list is still NOT established; only their shapes are. PARTLY RESOLVED by objectives_draw_category (formerly objective_status_text), which prints these records on the objectives screen - THE RECORDS ARE MISSION OBJECTIVES. The state byte at +0 reads 'Successful' at 5, 'Failed' at 6 and 'In progress' for anything else, 7 included. The byte at +1 is the category that the screen's caller filters on; objective_debug_view prints the game's own names for it: 1 Primary, 2 Secondary, 8 Return, anything else Tertiary (the data also uses 4 and 0). A non-zero byte at +0x5c means the objective is listed at all, and its text is at +0x95, continuing at +0xb5 past 32 characters. objective_table_install fills all of these from the static record - see missionTables for that layout. The flags dword at +2 is the objective's TYPE: objective_evaluate (formerly mission_result_sub_016720), which evaluates objectives, switches on it. What each type code means is still not established. PARTLY ESTABLISHED from the evaluator's clean branches, where 'targets' are the ushort entries from +0xd7, each {index, kind} with kind 1 tracked object, 2 mech, 4 gamething. Types 1 and 2 need every target destroyed, per objective_target_destroyed. Type 8 needs every target identified, per objective_target_identified. Type 0x20 needs every target identified AND every other objective whose +0x5d flag - the static record's 'M' - is set to be Successful (state 5); so M marks the objectives a type-0x20 objective waits for. Type 0x100 needs every target REACHED - the group leader within range, per objective_target_reached - and for any group but the player's, only while this objective is the one that group is working on, 0xd3ff0[group], so AI groups take their nav objectives in order. Type 0x2000 is its inverse: no target within range. Type 4 and code 0x10 are handled too, through register noise that has not been untangled. (Untangled since: see OUTCOMES below.) So has the second code the evaluator switches on, whose values 0x10000..0x100000 act on ANOTHER objective named by the ushorts at +0x91/+0x93: set its table's byte at 0xa5788 to 2 or 3, toggle its listed flag, or force it Failed (0x80000) or Successful (0x100000). The time test compares the dword at +0x57 - from the static +0x2a, -1 for none - against missionSeconds minus a start stamp at +0x4f - all in whole SECONDS. OUTCOMES, from objective_evaluate's disassembly (0x16abb..0x16e67). The type code is ONE dword: the C shows a second switch variable, but it is the same [record + 2] loaded again. Each evaluation starts the state at 3, in progress. The CONDITION types (1, 2, 8, 0x10, 0x20, 0x100, 0x2000) go Successful (5) when the condition holds and Failed (6) when it does not and the time limit has run out, so the limit is a deadline; 0x10 tests no targets, so it succeeds on its first evaluation. The TIMER types 0, 0x200, 0x400 and 0x800 go Successful once the time limit has run out and test nothing else. Type 4 is PROTECT: before the time runs out, losing any target fails it at once - 6 for the player's group, 8 for other groups - and when the time runs out it succeeds if every target survived. The ACTION types resolve another objective or table and then succeed themselves: 0x10000 sets the named table's objectiveTableResult to 2 (mission successful) and 0x20000 to 3 (mission failed), 0x40000 toggles the named objective's listed flag, and 0x80000 and 0x100000 force it Failed or Successful unless it is already finished. On any state change the dword at +0x53 is stamped with missionSeconds. Type 0x1000, used by 5 of the 2720 records in MW2.PRJ, falls through both switches untested and so succeeds on its first evaluation. How often each type is used, over the MTBL chunks the game actually loads (tools/dump_objectives.py walks BWD resources and their chunk streams): 311 tables, 2059 objectives - 0x2 508, 0x100 338, 0x10 311 (one per table, as it must be), 0x200 276, 0x400 133, 0x4 114, 0x2000 97, 0x100000 71, 0x20000 57, 0x40000 52, 0x80000 38, 0x800 27, 0x8 13, 0x20 12, 0x10000 9, 0x1000 3; type 1 never occurs. CORRECTION: an earlier version of this note gave 2720 records (0x2 681, 0x100 461, 0x10 408, ...). Those counts came from searching MW2.PRJ's bytes for 'MTBL' - exactly the scan CLAUDE.md warns against. 661 of the 2720 records sit in FREE resources, stale copies of old mission data left in the container's freed space, which the game never loads. The ranking survived; every count was inflated by about a third. The start stamp at +0x4f is taken, and the byte at +0x5b set, the first time an active objective is evaluated. EMPTY TARGET LISTS, from the same disassembly: the condition flag starts at 1 (mov ebx, 1 at 0x16756) and each target can only clear it, so with no targets every AND-over-targets condition holds. A destroy (1, 2), identify (8) or reach (0x100) objective with an empty list therefore SUCCEEDS on its first active evaluation. For an AI group, reach additionally needs to be that group's current objective, which seeds the flag. Protect (4) keeps a second flag, 'every target destroyed', also starting at 1 ([ebp-0x1c]). Empty, it is still 1, so before the deadline an empty protect objective goes to 6 at once, silently, through 0x16e1e -> 0x16e24, with no mission_result_format call. After the deadline, the all-alive branch makes it 5 first. WHICH OBJECTIVES THIS HITS (tools/dump_objective_targets.py): 229 destroy objectives get no targets in MW2.PRJ - the 226 named UserStar or en01star..en05star, which name no stream, and Goldare2, whose stream places nothing of its type - plus 2 reach objectives. All of them complete the moment they activate. No protect objective is empty in the shipped data.

groupCurrentObjective.doc: one dword per objective table, i.e. per group: the index of the objective the group is currently working on, or -1. mission_results_update recomputes it every frame as the first objective that is active (objective_is_active) and whose type's high word is 0, so not one of the 0x10000+ action types. When it changes it calls group_objective_changed (formerly ai_combat_sub_023a90)(table). The evaluator's type-0x100 (reach) branch uses it so AI groups take nav objectives in order

missionSeconds.doc: whole seconds of mission time: all three writers - mission_clock_update, mission_results_update (formerly exit_prompt) and objective_table_start (formerly game_boot_sub_015f60) - store simTick / 0xb6, and 0xb6 is 182 ticks, one second. Objective time limits (the static record's +0x2a) and the start and completion stamps are all in this unit. The shipped limits confirm it: whole-second values from 0 to 310, most often 0, 30, 1, 5 and 20, -1 meaning none - counted by tools/dump_objectives.py over the objectives the game loads. An earlier version of this note quoted '5, 10, 15, 30, 45 and 60' from a byte scan that also counted stale FREE-space copies; see the correction on missionRecordState

missionTableCount.doc: how many missionTables slots are live; both record searches bound their outer loop with it rather than with the array size of sixteen

uiContextTail.doc: tail of the same list - ui_context_register links each new node through this one's +0xe before taking its place

uiContextHead.doc: head of the ui context list ui_context_register builds. Every walker in project_tables starts here and follows the next link at +0xe

menuOpenCount.doc: menus open: menu_open increments it, menu_close decrements it; ui_context_request_open and ui_context_toggle only open a menu while it is 0

menuKeyPending.doc: the key code menu_poll_key leaves for the menu code to consume - 0x0d from menu_enter, 0x1b from menu_abort, 0x96/0x97 and 0x99/0x20 from the two analog menu axes, or a raw keystroke passed through from playerControls +0x14

fleeToDos.doc: set by menu_item_flee_to_dos; main then exits with code 0xff instead of 0

devDirEntries.doc: the name set's entry pool: 200 entries of 0x14 bytes, a 16-byte file name then the next-in-chain pointer at +0x10 (0xd4094 for entry 0). project_add_entry hands them out in order, and 200 is the system_error limit

devDirBuckets.doc: 101 chain heads of the name set project_add_entry maintains over the files in devDirPath: the hash is taken mod 0x65 and each bucket holds a pointer to the most recently added entry

devDirPath.doc: the path of the developer content directory: project_scan_dev_dir sprintfs '%s%s' of an optional drive prefix and the literal 'keating' into it at startup and scans it. The drive prefix is a letter and ':' when sound_seq_sub_0423f0 returns a drive number rather than -1, and empty otherwise. dev_dir_load_sfl builds the path of an .sfl file under it. No keating directory ships with the game

animCache.doc: up to sixty loaded animations, as interleaved pairs eight bytes apart: the id at +0 and the slot it was given at +4. anim_ensure_loaded searches the ids linearly and appends on a miss. The pairing is why the exported source shows two globals eight bytes apart being indexed by i * 2 - 0xd52b8 and 0xd52bc are the two halves of one array, not two arrays

mechLastAnimState.doc: one int per mech, indexed by MechEntity.index, holding the animState whose transition sound was played last. mech_play_anim_transition_sound is its only user: it refuses to play again while this still matches, writes animState here after playing, and writes -2 instead once animState and animTarget agree, so -2 means settled and nothing is pending. Without it a mech would retrigger its transition sound every frame.

altRootNode.doc: the second sentinel. object_link chooses it as the parent instead of worldRootNode when bit 0x1000 of the object flag word is set, and object_unlink refuses to unlink it exactly as it refuses worldRoot. WHAT BIT 0x1000 MEANS was not established; ONE SETTER IS KNOWN since: scenery_c0_set_visible(0) sets it on every family-0xc0 object (lights, *SPRS* meshes) it hides, so the altRoot list holds scenery switched off by a detail option. Whether anything else sets 0x1000 is NOT established - only that it selects this root

altListHead.doc: first object on altRootNode's list - altRootNode.listNext, reached as an absolute address like worldChainHead. object_move_to_alt_list and scenery_c0_set_visible's hide path push onto it; objects here have flags 0x1000 set and are out of the world list. object_lists_free_all frees whatever is left at shutdown

worldRootNode.doc: the sentinel object worldRoot points at, not a pointer itself. object_lists_reset (formerly terrain_sub_01f730) lays out THREE of these 20-byte headers - 0xf44ac, 0xf44c0 and 0xf44d4 - zeroing their links and giving each the flag word 0x4000. This one does double duty in object_link: it is the default parent in the child list AND the sentinel the world chain hangs off. The third, 0xf44d4, is initialised and then read by nothing

worldListHead.doc: first object on worldRootNode's list - worldRootNode.listNext. object_move_to_world_list pushes onto it, scenery_c0_set_visible walks it as the objects in the world, and object_lists_free_all frees it at shutdown

worldChainHead.doc: first object on the world chain. PHYSICALLY THIS IS worldRootNode + 0x10, the sentinel own next field - the compiler reached it as an absolute address, so it prints as a separate global. Reading it as an independent variable would hide that the chain is rooted in the sentinel

auxRootNode.doc: the THIRD sentinel of the three object_lists_reset lays out (after altRootNode at 0xf44ac and worldRootNode at 0xf44c0), born with flag 0x4000 like the others; its listNext word is 0xf44dc. object_move_to_aux_list pushes objects onto the list it heads, and scene_subtree_move_to_aux_list does so for a whole model - the one vfx_video_sub_0103c0 finds as the first family-0x90 object. What the list is used for is NOT established

auxListHead.doc: first object on auxRootNode's list - auxRootNode.listNext; object_move_to_aux_list pushes onto it and object_lists_free_all frees it at shutdown

aiRuleTables.doc: ten pointer slots holding the nine AIT resources ai_rule_tables_load fetches at startup, ids 1..9; slot 0 is zeroed and never filled. ai_set_state_rule_block is the only reader - it copies one of these pointers into a MechEntity.stateRules block, which is what identifies an AIT resource as a block of AI rules

heatWarningTick.doc: simTick when heatWarningLatch was set; mech_heat_update re-arms the warning 0x2d8 ticks after it, once heat is below 66 percent

formationPresets.doc: 0x20 StarFormation rows, copied wholesale into formationTable[group] by group_set_formation, whose guard is value < 0x20. The row count is not guessed: 0x20 rows of 0x4c ends at 0xfc604, which is exactly where affiliationAllegiance, the table MechGroup.affiliation indexes, begins. The rows are zero in the image - they are BSS, filled at load time from the project file, and group_set_formation_by_name then finds one by strcmp on its leading name.

fallingObjects.doc: 128 slots of 0x21 bytes for scene nodes under simple physics - TYPED as FallingObject[128] by applyFallingObjects; the struct's field notes are the current word, and the offsets below are the history of how they were reached. Per slot: +0x00 a byte, +0x01 the SceneNode * that also keys it, +0x09 the vertical velocity, +0x1d the acceleration added to that velocity each tick, and five more words at +0x05, +0x0d, +0x11, +0x15 and +0x19 that the bounce halves and negates. +0x05 and +0x0d are the X and Z velocity beside +0x09's vertical one: falling_object_push adds an impulse to exactly those three, and caps them as one vector. RESOLVED. An earlier pass called these the linear and angular components of a tumble but could not say which was which, and also miscounted them as four. falling_object_randomise_motion splits them, because it initialises the two groups with DIFFERENT formulas: +0x05, +0x09 and +0x0d each take a random scaled by 0x57e98 over gravitySetting, while +0x11, +0x15 and +0x19 each take a random times 0x7e98 over 0x400. +0x09 is already known independently to be the vertical velocity, and it sits in the first group - so +0x05, +0x09 and +0x0d are the LINEAR velocity triple and +0x11, +0x15 and +0x19 the ANGULAR one. A second sign agrees: of the six, only +0x09 has a bias added to its random before scaling, so debris is thrown upward on average. A linear velocity does that; an angular one has no reason to. falling_object_tick integrates each slot and tests the result against the terrain height; contact damps it, and a slow enough bounce frees the node subtree and releases the slot. The acceleration at +0x1d IS gravity, which a previous pass could only infer from the terrain-contact test: falling_object_attach initialises it to -gravity, the same global the mech movement integration uses as its vertical acceleration. The byte at +0x00 is a kind supplied by the caller - destructible_register passes 2, the other two callers pass 1 - and what the two kinds mean is not established. This is NOT the destructibles table, though the two are related: destructible_register takes a slot here for every object it registers, and destructible_destroy searches this table for the slot whose node matches the one it is blowing up and clears it. destructibles_update walks both, one loop each.

destructibles.doc: 128 slots of 17 bytes for the scenery that can be shot to pieces - TYPED as Destructible[128] by applyDestructibles, whose field notes are the current word. CORRECTION to what follows: +0x0d is not only run 'when it dies' but on every release (see Destructible.onRelease), and destructibles_blast_damage belongs in the interface list - it reads and writes hit points directly. Per slot: +0x00 a byte, 0 free and 1 live; +0x01 the SceneNode * holding its geometry; +0x05 the simTick it was registered; +0x09 hit points in 16.16, starting at 0x100000; +0x0d a callback run when it dies, passed the node. A freed slot is restored from the 17-byte template at 0x96360, which is what fixes the stride. The units are not inferred: projectile_update damages a slot with Projectile.damage << 0x10, so a fresh object takes 16 points in the same scale the weapon table uses. destructible_register, destructible_apply_damage, destructible_destroy, destructibles_update and destructibles_reset are the whole interface, and every access to the table is inside ai_group_part2.

aiBehaviourSets.doc: AiBehaviourSet[8], indexed by MechEntity.gamepieceClass - 1; filled once per run by ai_behaviour_init, read by ai_choose_behaviour

aiBehaviourSetElemental.doc: the set ai_choose_behaviour uses instead of aiBehaviourSets when loadout->tons == 1 - only the ELE00SPC and ELE00STD chassis

damageColourRemap.doc: byte[256], a palette translation table. hud_damage_display_init fills it with the identity; hud_damage_diagram_draw writes the damage colour into entry 6 before redrawing each region through it, so only pixels of palette index 6 in the diagram shape change colour

hiddenText.doc: the HTXT ('hidden_text') chunk's string, copied from +8 by project_chunk_exec at 0x4e71b. Its one consumer is hud_target_readout_tick: for a gamething that is not identified (flags 0x20 clear) but has flags 0x100, the readout shows this instead of the thing's name, and first fills it with 'Unknown' if it is empty. One global, so the last HTXT chunk run wins. MW2.PRJ has 18: 'Empty' in 13, 'Nothing' in 4, 'Jammed' in GOLDWLD1. Whether it is ever shown depends on GameThing.flags 0x100, for which no source was found

playerStatusCopy.doc: the player's MechLoadout.status (+0xa0: 2 running, 3 shut down, 4 and 5 destroyed), copied every frame by the per-frame HUD dispatcher player_cockpit_frame (formerly sound_res_sub_032c50) for the player's loadout while 0x9626c is set - it reads param_1[0x28] and skips the rest of its work at 4 or 5. The HUD widget ticks store it at their +0x3c and hud_widget13_tick only renders the target view at 2; the dispatcher only honours punchInAutoHeadingRequest (formerly faceLegsToTorsoRequest) at 2

cachePurgeHead.doc: the most recently unlocked item. cache_unlock pushes here, and an item with locked == 0 is on this list and nowhere else. It is the newest end of an LRU list

cachePurgeTail.doc: the item unlocked longest ago, and the next one evicted: cache_load_resource hands it to cache_free_item when the cache is full or malloc fails. When it is 0 and something must go, the result is 'CACHE FULL - Nothing to purge' or 'Memory running low'

cacheItemCount.doc: items in the cache. cache_load_resource increments it and cache_free_item decrements it. A load evicts cachePurgeTail first when this is over 999, so the cache holds at most 1000 items whatever their size

polyDrawList.doc: 8-byte {draw record, depth key} pairs, one per visible polygon, appended by the clipper (poly_clip_and_queue), sorted by depth_pairs_sort_desc and drawn in that order by poly_emit_screen_vertices - DESCENDING depth, farthest first. So MW2 draws polygons back to front (a painter's algorithm) with no depth buffer; a port that uses one differs only where that order matters, e.g. overlap between objects

walkDrawList.doc: 8-byte {entry, depth} pairs filled during render_object_list's object walk, when drawListCurrent points here: the clipper appends every visible polygon's draw record (key from polySortFlags), and render_object_list appends each object with flags bit 0x100 together with objectViewDepth. render_draw_depth_sorted sorts it descending and tells the two apart by bit 0x8000 of the entry's first word (set on every WorldObject, never in a record's vertex count). THE TWO KINDS OF KEY ARE ON DIFFERENT SCALES. A polygon's key comes from its vertices' cached view depth (vertex +0x20), which the clipper computes as (world - viewTranslation) . viewDepthRow >> 27 - FOUR TIMES centimetres, the scale viewNearClipScaled and viewFarClipScaled (x 4) exist for. An object's key is objectViewDepth, which object_cull_main_view computes with the same rows >> 29 (shrd esi, edi, 0x1d at 0x3f5fa) - plain centimetres, compared with the unscaled viewNearClip. So a 0x100 object at distance D sorts with key D against polygons whose keys are 4 x their distance: it is drawn after every ordinary polygon farther than D/4, as if it were at a quarter of its distance, and tends to paint over ordinary geometry around it. Its own polygons are then re-sorted among themselves with consistent x4 keys, and its LOD choice uses the centimetre depth, which is consistent too. Whether the factor was intended is not established; a port reproducing MW2's ordering must compare the object's depth x1 against polygon depths x4. IN THE SHIPPED DATA NO OBJECT CARRIES 0x100, so this path is never exercised. An object gets it only through its load flags (object_apply_load_flags), and every source of those is accounted for: OBJ chunks (+0x32) - none of the 12182 in MW2.PRJ sets 0x100; world records, whose flags bits 0-8 are that same OBJ value (project_obj_exec pushes local_2c, the chunk's +0x32, as world_record_define's flags argument - [ebp'+0x5a] with ebp' = ebp - 0x86, the frame the rep movsd of the chunk's +0xe block at 0x4e282 fixes); detail_record_build passes 0 and quadtree_debug_draw 4. So in practice walkDrawList holds only polygon records, and the x4 key mismatch never arises; a port can treat 0x100 as unused, or implement it as the code does. CORRECTION: this was named deferredObjectList, described as holding only the 0x100 objects' pairs

frameArenaBase.doc: start of the per-frame arena render_buffers_init allocates; frame_arena_reset puts frameArenaLow back here

frameArenaHigh.doc: the arena's falling cursor: clip records (frame_arena_alloc_clip, 0x20 bytes) are taken from here downwards. frame_arena_reset sets it to base + size - 0x30. render_buffers_init sets it DIFFERENTLY: base + (frameArenaBytes << 5) - 0x600, i.e. base + 32 * (size - 0x30) - read from the disassembly (shl eax, 5 / add eax, [frameArenaBase] / add eax, 0xfffffa00 at 0x33fc7..0x33fd5). That is what C pointer arithmetic gives for (32-byte clip record *)base + size - 0x30, so it looks like a slip in the original source, and it points far past the arena. It is harmless only because render_object_list and render_scene_tree_sorted call frame_arena_reset before they allocate anything; a port should use the reset value

frameArenaLow.doc: the arena's rising cursor: draw records (frame_arena_alloc_draw, 0xc bytes plus the polygon's clip-record pointers copied after it) are taken from here upwards

drawListCapacity.doc: entries in polyDrawList and walkDrawList: maxPolygons from render_buffers_init, 0x5dc (1500) in the game

sinTable.doc: 256 sine entries plus two guard slots, built at startup by math_build_trig_tables and read by fixed_sin as a base value and its neighbour for interpolation. The guard slots hold 0x20000000, so the scale is 2^29 and not 16.16 - which is why vec_to_range_bearing shifts its dividend left by 29 before dividing by a sine.
