THE RECIPE, read from math_build_trig_tables' disassembly (0x3aa90..0x3ab1f): [i] = trunc(sin(i * K) * 2^29) for i = 0..255, with K the double at 0x90fac, 0.00613592314453125 - pi/512 rounded - so the 256 entries are a quarter wave; trunc is clib_fp_trunc, rounding toward zero. tools/dump_trig_tables.py regenerates the table from the constants in the code and checks the guard (listing/trig_tables.txt).

atanTable.doc: 256 arctangent entries plus two guard slots, in the same 16.16 degrees as every other angle in the sim. fixed_atan2 indexes it with a ratio that is always in 0..1, so it only has to cover the first 45 degrees; the guard slots hold 0x2d0000, which is atan(1) = 45 degrees. THE RECIPE (same disassembly as sinTable): [i] = trunc(atan(i / 256) * K) for i = 0..255, with K the double at 0x90fc4, 3754936.21046 - which is 65536 * 180 / pi = 3754936.20617 STORED SLIGHTLY LARGE, by about 1.1e-9 relative; the table follows the stored value. See tools/dump_trig_tables.py.

sqrtTable.doc: 1024 ushorts, sqrtTable[i] = trunc(sqrt(i) * 1024), built once by sqrt_table_build with the x87. The integer-only square root for vector normalisation: triangle_normal indexes it with the high word of a sum of squares >> 4. Like sinTable and atanTable, it exists so the per-frame maths never touches the FPU

sqrtTablePtr.doc: the address of sqrtTable, stored by sqrt_table_build; triangle_normal and poly_light_intensity (formerly render_asm_sub_03e086) read the table through it

cosAtanTable.doc: int[800], 2.29 fixed point: [i] = trunc(2^29 / sqrt(1 + (i/16)^2)), i.e. cos(atan(i / 16)). Filled once by atan_sincos_tables_init. The constants are doubles in the image: 0.0625 at 0x90fcc, 2^29 at 0x90fd4. Indexed by a TANGENT in 1/16 steps, clamped to 799 (a tangent under 50). Its only reader is viewer_update_projection. 0x320 entries end exactly at sinAtanTable

sinAtanTable.doc: int[800], 2.29: [i] = trunc(2^29 * (i/16) / sqrt(1 + (i/16)^2)) = sin(atan(i / 16)); see cosAtanTable. The x87 sequence at 0x3ab2c..0x3ab62 computes 1/sqrt(1+t^2) once and multiplies it by 2^29 for this table's neighbour and by t * 2^29 for this one

dataSelector3.doc: the third copy of DS from that sequence. Nothing outside realmode_selectors_create touches it

dataSelector2.doc: a second copy of the same DS value, written by the same three-store sequence. netplay re-copies dataSelector into it. WHY THERE ARE THREE COPIES IS NOT ESTABLISHED - they are written identically and only diverge if something rewrites one

biosDataSelector.doc: the selector for real-mode segment 0x0040, the BIOS data area. Built and freed alongside the other two; NO READER has been found, so what the game wanted the BIOS data area for is not established

vgaSelector.doc: the protected-mode selector realmode_selectors_create builds for real-mode segment 0xa000, the VGA framebuffer. video_init copies it into the selector field of the canvas record at 0xa46f8, beside a malloc'd buffer of width x height - which is what identifies it as the screen rather than any other mapping

monoSelector.doc: the selector for real-mode segment 0xb000, the monochrome adapter's text buffer. debug_text_draw loads it into ES and stosw's character/attribute cells through it, which is only visible in the disassembly - the C body appears to write to absolute low addresses. The developer HUD therefore went to a second, monochrome monitor. CAUTION: this global was previously described in debug_text_draw as a flag, because the C shows only a non-zero test

dataSelector.doc: a copy of DS, taken with segread at the end of realmode_selectors_create. video_init copies it into a second canvas record at 0xa4700 - the one whose pixels live in main memory rather than at 0xa000, which is the distinction between this and vgaSelector

projectBlockFrames.doc: 32 block frames of 0x7c bytes, indexed by slot rather than by depth - TYPED as ProjectBlockFrame[32] by applyBlockFrames. project_block_begin copies fields out of the BLK chunk into one of these. The bound of 32 rests on the slot guard, which tests against 0x20, and the stride of 0x7c. CORRECTION: this note said 32 x 0x7c 'ends exactly where projectBlockStack starts', as a third corroboration. It does not: 32 x 0x7c is 0xf80, so the frames end at 0x101d90 and projectBlockStack is at 0x101e10, 0x80 bytes later. The arithmetic had been done as if 32 x 0x7c were 0x1000. The gap 0x101d90..0x101e0f is referenced by no instruction in any function - a sweep of every function's operands finds nothing there - so the 0x80 bytes are unused, and the bound of 32 rests on the guard alone

projectBlockStack.doc: one slot index per open block, indexed by projectBlockDepth - the stack that says which frame each depth is using

worldRecordMapCount.doc: live entries in the world record map; world_record_alloc appends while it is below worldRecordMapCapacity

worldRecordsDirty.doc: set to 1 by world_records_propagate - its only writer of 1, at all three places where it changes a child's state; world_records_tick runs world_records_propagate only while it is set, then clears it (xor ebx,ebx before the call, stored after). So propagation reruns every frame until a pass changes nothing

detailMapCapacity.doc: the bound on detailMapCount, and the length an outermost REPR resets detailMapValues over

detailMapCount.doc: live entries in the detail map. Zeroed by an outermost REPR and raised by project_obj_exec for every OBJ inside one, while below detailMapCapacity

bitmap3dTable.doc: 512 Bitmap3dSlot records driving what the project vocabulary calls 3dbitmaps - frame animations whose frames are resources in bitmap3dFrames blocks. The 512 comes from BMID bounds-checking both its arguments against 0x200; the 14-byte stride from the indexing. Previous note, kept because the field names below replace it:

savedViewPose.doc: 7 ints camera_missile_view saves on entry and restores on exit: posX, posY, posZ, yaw, pitch, roll of viewerPosition, then a valid flag at +0x18

camOrbitHeightMin.doc: 200 - mechTable[0]'s rideHeight: the lowest camOrbitHeight may go, about 2 m above the ground under a standing mech

drawListCurrent.doc: whichever list is being appended to: walkDrawList during render_object_list's walk, polyDrawList from render_draw_depth_sorted on and throughout render_scene_tree_sorted (formerly render_asm_sub_03d170)'s walk; drawListCount indexes it

frameHasRoom.doc: 1 while this frame can still take polygons. Set to 1 at the start of each object walk (render_object_list, render_scene_tree_sorted (formerly render_asm_sub_03d170)); cleared by frame_arena_alloc_clip and frame_arena_alloc_draw when the arena's two cursors come within 0xc8 bytes, and by the clipper when polyDrawList is full (drawListCount >= drawListCapacity). Its readers stop walking objects once it is 0, so an overfull frame silently DROPS the remaining objects rather than failing

objectViewDepth.doc: the view-space depth of the object last passed to object_view_cull: (position - viewTranslation) dotted with the depth row, in cm, growing away from the eye. render_object_list hands it to object_draw_lod_mesh as the LOD distance and records it with deferred objects for render_draw_depth_sorted. In the main view its writer is object_cull_main_view (0x3f60f), from the rows >> 29 (0x3f5fa), so it is in centimetres - a QUARTER of the scale of the polygon depth keys it is sorted against in walkDrawList; see there

polySortFlags.doc: the flags word of the object being drawn, latched by render_object_list (0x3cfb3) for the polygon clipper, which reads bits 0-2 to build each polygon's depth-sort key: 0x2 mean depth, else 0x4 minimum, else maximum, and 0x1 ORs 0x40000000 (draw first, always behind). Its only writer is render_object_list, so polygons reached through render_scene_tree_sorted (formerly render_asm_sub_03d170)'s walk use whatever it last latched

paletteResourceIds.doc: twenty resource ids, one per palette slot; every palette load in render_asm is cache_load_resource(.., paletteResourceIds[slot], ..). The count is the 0x14 the init pass fills and palette_slot_set_resource swaps one entry

viewportModes.doc: 11 records of five ints - the bound viewport_select enforces is index < 0xb, and every user indexes at stride 5. Ints 1..4 are a rectangle: viewport_select takes [3] - [1] and [4] - [2] as the width and height it gives the viewer. What int 0 holds is not established. RESOLVED: each record is a ViewWindow {canvas, left, top, right, bottom} - see buildViewWindow for the evidence; typed ViewWindow[11] now. THE DATA: MW2.PRJ has ONE VWSP chunk, in the MW2MECH stream, defining windows 0..7 of a 320x200 screen as {index, x, y, width, height, 0, 0, 0} - the last three dwords are 0 in all eight and the reader never looks at them. 0: 0,0 320x200, the full screen, which vfx_video selects by default. 1: 0,16 320x178. 2: 0,25 320x150. 3: 0,33 320x133 - three shrinking letterboxes of the main view, reached through the index at 0x954f4 that vfx_video_sub_010490 selects when it is non-zero. CORRECTION: they are NOT reached in practice - that index (mainViewWindow) is 0 in the data and its only writer is dead code, so windows 1..3 are defined but never selected. 4: 80,50 160x100, centred - its user is not established. 5: 258,145 52x34, lower right - hud_widget02_tick renders the player's own mech into it (render_view_from_pose(5, ...), damageDisplayMode 3..5). 6: 13,10 67x50, upper left - user not established. 7: 10,145 52x34, lower left - hud_widget13_tick renders the player's target into it (render_view_from_pose(7, ...), framed on targetX/Y/Z with sky and ground off). Windows 8..10 get nothing from the shipped data (VWSP would accept 8, not 9 or 10). They keep what video_init put there: it calls viewport_windows_reset (formerly render_asm_sub_03e5b0), which copies currentViewport - the full screen at that point - into all 11 slots before any VWSP runs. vfx_video also copies HUD window records in, at indices those records carry, which were not traced for this note.

paletteFadeState.doc: the interpolator clib_sub_063a70 fills - three 0x300-byte arrays, which is 256 entries x 3 components, and the reason this block is a PALETTE rather than any other 0x100-element table

paletteCycleState.doc: the colour-cycling block palette_cycle_setup would fill: {palette, copy, first byte, count at +9}; nothing fills it

viewProjShiftX.doc: Viewer.projShiftX - viewer_project_point shifts left by it, the unproject path shifts right

viewProjScaleX.doc: Viewer.projScaleX latched by viewer_latch_globals and folded into the row 0 matrix globals

viewProjScaleY.doc: Viewer.projScaleY, folded into the row 1 matrix globals

viewCentreX.doc: written by viewer_latch_globals from Viewer.centreX; viewer_project_point adds it to the projected x

cullRow1X.doc: Viewer.rotation[3], copied by viewer_latch_globals; with cullRow1Y/Z at +4/+8 it is rotation row 1, the second lateral axis

cullDepthRowX.doc: Viewer.rotation[6], rotation row 2, the depth axis. viewer_latch_globals writes the same value to viewDepthRowX in the next statement; the cull hooks read this copy

cullRow0X.doc: Viewer.rotation[0], copied by viewer_latch_globals; with cullRow0Y/Z at +4/+8 it is rotation row 0, the first lateral axis the cull hooks project onto

viewTranslationY.doc: written by viewer_latch_globals from Viewer.translationY - note it sits BELOW the x copy

viewTranslationX.doc: written by viewer_latch_globals from Viewer.translationX; read by viewer_project_point

viewLeft.doc: written by viewer_latch_globals from Viewer.left; the four bounds are the on-screen test in viewer_project_point

viewFarClip.doc: Viewer.farClip latched for the render pipeline

viewDepthRowZ.doc: written by viewer_latch_globals from Viewer.rotation[8] unscaled

viewDepthRowY.doc: written by viewer_latch_globals from Viewer.rotation[7] unscaled

viewNearClipScaled.doc: viewNearClip x 4 - the form viewer_project_point (formerly render_asm_sub_03f320) compares vertex depth against

viewNearClip.doc: Viewer.nearClip latched for the render pipeline by viewer_latch_globals

viewFarClipScaled.doc: viewFarClip x 4, saturated to INT_MAX by viewer_set_far_clip

cullDepthRowY.doc: Viewer.rotation[7] - see cullDepthRowX; equal to viewDepthRowY

cullDepthRowZ.doc: Viewer.rotation[8] - see cullDepthRowX; equal to viewDepthRowZ

viewDepthRowX.doc: written by viewer_latch_globals from Viewer.rotation[6] unscaled - the row that yields view-space depth

cameraKeyIndex.doc: the keyframe playing. camera_keys_start sets 0, camera_keys_update increments it when cameraKeyElapsed reaches the keyframe's ticks and drops cameraKeysActive once it runs off the end or goes negative

cameraKeyElapsed.doc: ticks spent in the current keyframe: camera_keys_update adds tickDelta each frame and resets it to 0 on advancing. READING NOTE: midi_open (formerly sound_seq_sub_041260) renders as (&cameraKeyElapsed)[i] = -1 for i = 1..8. That is not this variable - the instruction is mov [eax*4 + 0x15006c] with eax starting at 1, so it writes 0x150070..0x15008c, a separate eight-entry sound table whose one-based index the compiler folded into the displacement

voiceLines.doc: the eight VoiceLine records sound_seq_queue_message allocates from

cdTrackFirst.doc: the lowest track number the play path accepts - cd_track_in_range's lower bound and the base the play routine subtracts before indexing the per-track table at 0x15035c. Presumably filled from MSCDEX's audio disk info, but that writer was not read

cdTrackLast.doc: the highest track number cd_track_in_range accepts; see cdTrackFirst

enemyLockWarnTick.doc: sound_frame_update's next check, every 0x38e ticks (5 s): SNDS 0x100 plays when an enemy in aiState 2 or 3 has the player as targetSecondary within 0x249f0 cm

soundSettings.doc: 1200 x 8 bytes indexed by SNDS id: +0 priority (sound_channel_start passes it to sound_sample_open, which only steals a channel playing at lower priority), +2 maxPlaying (sound_sample_open refuses a sound already playing that many times; -1 no limit), +4 playback rate (-1 = soundRateTable[5], 11025 Hz), +6 how many are playing now. Filled by sound_settings_init

videoDriverFlags.doc: bit 0 is set by the -VG command-line option. vfx_load_drivers then loads the video driver named in videoDriverName, or runs vfx\vfxscan.dll to find one when that is empty; without the bit it loads mcga.dll. main SETS it first, before the command line is parsed, from the options block at *0x97e3c: 0, then 1 when +0xb holds a driver name - the saved setting - so -VG only adds to what the options file chose

videoDriverName.doc: char[12], the name after -VG= (strncpy 0xc), or empty for a bare -VG. main fills it first from the options block's +0xb, except that the name 'scan' (stricmp) leaves it empty, which is what makes vfx_load_drivers autodetect with vfxscan.dll. vfx_load_drivers loads it as the video driver

netOpponentAnnounced.doc: int[8], per station: set when netplay_apply_state first sees that station's mech at status 4 or 5 and posts 'Opponent mech %i destroyed.', so it is posted once

netStationFlags.doc: int[8], one per network station, read in netplay_frame_exchange, netplay_join and netplay_sign_off: bit 2 = this round's packet was delivered to it (net_send returned 0), bit 4 = something was heard from it this round, 0x1f = the station is gone (signed off, or unused above the station count). The round bits are cleared at the start of each exchange for every station with nothing in 0xf0; netplay_elect_master picks the lowest station with nothing in 0xf0

netRecvBufferLinear.doc: linear address (segment << 4) of the real-mode receive buffer net_next_message walks

netSendBufferLinear.doc: linear address (segment << 4) of the real-mode send buffer, where net_queue_message builds the outgoing packet

netMyStation.doc: short: this machine's station number, from net_station_info's high byte. netplay_init copies it into playerMechIndex - a station drives the mech of its own number

netMasterStation.doc: short: the station that owns the clock - the lowest one not gone (netplay_elect_master). Only its DA packets carry simTick

cheatKeyHistory.doc: the last fourteen keystrokes, shifted left by one each time a key arrives so the newest sits at the end. cheat_match compares backwards from there, which makes any code a suffix match.

monoDebugPresent.doc: 1 once a monochrome debug display has been found: its only writer, input_sub_049050, sets it when project_file_sub_04af3c's probe succeeds, then turns the cursor off through the 6845 CRTC at port 0x3b4 (project_file_sub_04b039), clears the 2000-cell 80x25 buffer (project_file_sub_04afff) and sets hangAround. Every debug_text_draw overlay - ai_debug_mech_table and the mission_log and main ones - is gated on it. The mono selector itself is monoSelector

randomNextTable.doc: the other 127 ints, 0x152e00..0x152ff8, read ONE-BASED by random_next - the label sits one entry below the data, which is what makes the 1..127 index land in range. random_tables_init fills it differently from randomRangeTable: it spins the Miles RNG thirty times per entry and rounds a long double through clib_fp_trunc (formerly clib_core_sub_05c3c2). WHY THE TWO TABLES ARE BUILT DIFFERENTLY IS NOT ESTABLISHED

randomRangeTable.doc: 127 ints, 0x152ffc..0x1531f4, read 0-based by random_range. random_tables_init fills it straight from the Miles RNG. Its base prints as DAT_00152ff8 inside the initialiser because that loop indexes from 1

projectFiles.doc: TYPED as ProjectFile[1] by applyProjectFiles - the capacity is 1, from project_file_open's slot loop (cmp edx, 1 at 0x4a399). the per-open-file records, stride 0x14a. The file handle sits here at +0; project_load_directories seeks and reads through it. CORRECTION: a previous pass put this label at 0x153206 and quoted the other fields relative to THAT, calling the header pointer field 0 and the type-directory slots +0x24. Those offsets were self-consistent but mis-based by 6 bytes - 0x153206 is the header pointer, not the start of the record. Whether the record truly begins at 0x153200 is still NOT established; that is only the lowest field seen so far. RESOLVED by project_close and project_file_proj_handler: both form the address of the name as mov eax, 0x153200 / add eax, record offset / add eax, 0x12a (0x4a62e and 0x4a542). That is the compiler's &record + offsetof(name), so 0x153200 is the base it used. Layout, all 0x14a bytes accounted for: +0x00 handle, +0x04 projectFileInUse, +0x06 projectFileHeaders, +0x0a..0x29 UNREAD by any function Ghidra knows, +0x2a 32 type slots of 8 bytes (projectTypeDirs, projectTypeAux), +0x12a projectFileName[0x20]

projectFileInUse.doc: ushort at +0x04 of each projectFiles record. project_file_open (formerly project_file_proj_handler) refuses to open (returns -1) when it is non-zero and sets it to 1 after a successful load; project_close clears it. Note that the handler's search only ever inspects record 0, so in practice there is one project file slot

projectFileHeaders.doc: now ProjectFile.header, typed ProjectHeader *. pointer to the loaded file header, at +6 of each projectFiles record. The header holds a ushort type count at +0xc and then that many 0x18-byte type entries from +0xe: tag at +0, directory file offset at +4 with zero meaning the type has none, directory byte size at +8, and the ushort at +0x14 that BOTH project_resource_size and project_read_resource use - the reader adds it to the entry's start and subtracts it from the entry's length, which is the shape of skipping a fixed per-type prefix, RESOLVED - the prefix has now been seen. Every type uses base 62, and those 62 bytes are a record header: a DATA magic at +0, length - 8 at +4, the type tag again at +0xc, the resource id at +0x18 and a NUL-padded name at +0x1e. dump_project_index.py checks all five against every non-empty resource in MW2.PRJ and all 7073 pass, so the loader is skipping a per-record header and handing callers the payload alone. Bytes +0x08..0x0b and +0x10..0x17 vary per record and are still unidentified. A type's directory holds 8-byte entries from +0x16, each a start offset and a length

projectTypeDirs.doc: RENDERING CAVEAT: since the table was typed, this label sits inside an array, and readers that form the address as a plain integer (base + index * stride) now print the raw hex 0x15322a instead of this name - the decompiler neither resolves it to a field path nor falls back to the label in integer arithmetic. Before typing they printed (int)&projectTypeDirs + ... ; the typed readers gained field names, these lost the label. now ProjectFile.types[i].directory. one 8-byte slot per type, at +0x2a of each projectFiles record, holding that type's directory once project_load_directories has read it in. project_resource_size indexes a loaded directory as +0x1a + id * 8

projectTypeAux.doc: the second dword of each 8-byte projectTypeDirs slot, at +0x2e of the record. project_close frees it through projectFreeHook when non-null and zeroes it. A decoded-instruction sweep of every listed function finds NO OTHER READER OR WRITER, so what it holds, and whether anything ever fills it, is not established

projectFileName.doc: char[0x20] at +0x12a of each projectFiles record. project_file_open (formerly project_file_proj_handler) clears it and strncpy's the path it was asked to open into it, 0x20 bytes; project_close clears it again. No reader has been found

crashHandlerDS.doc: a 16-bit copy of the program's DS, saved by install_crash_handlers. The exception stubs load DS from it through a CS override, because DS is not guaranteed on entry to a DPMI exception handler

dtblCountAGP.doc: short, the running total of DTBL +0x08 over every file project_walk_chunks visits, INCL and GPS included. arena_budget_build multiplies it by 0x1ec for AGP and by mech_loadout_size for MGP - both per-mech sizes - and in MW2.PRJ it is 1 in each mech's gamepiece file. What the count means beyond feeding those two budgets is named by its consumer only. DTBL +0x0a, +0x10 and +0x12 are summed into 0x1534ba, 0x1534c0 and 0x1534c2 the same way and NOTHING READS THOSE three totals

dtblCountSEG.doc: short, running total of DTBL +0x0c; times scene_node_size for SEG

dtblCountOBJI.doc: short, running total of DTBL +0x0e; times 8 for OBJI and times 4 for both CID and CINS, so it sizes projectObjectMap and the world-record and detail maps together

dtblCountTLIS.doc: short, running total of DTBL +0x14; times task_node_size for TLIS and times 0x28 for ADAT, so every task budgets one ADAT record as well

dtblCountANTK.doc: short, running total of DTBL +0x16, times 0x14 for ANTK. Unlike the counts above, project_walk_chunks adds this and dtblBytesANFL only when stream_seen_find returns zero for the stream, and then calls stream_seen_add on it, so these two are counted once per DISTINCT stream rather than once per inclusion. RESOLVED: this note used to say the two functions (then screenshot_sub_04c650 and screenshot_sub_04c5d0) had not been read and that the shape only looked like a seen-before check. Both have now been read from the disassembly and it is one: a linked list of {id, name} stream references (streamSeenHead), matched by name for id -1/-2 and by id otherwise, and cleared by stream_seen_clear when project_load_by_name finishes. The list is per measurement, so 'distinct' means within one project_load_by_name walk

dtblBytesANFL.doc: int, running total of the DTBL dword at +0x18, used as the ANFL budget directly - a byte count, not a count of records - which fits res_load_anim passing ANFL as the arena for a whole-file load

streamSeenTail.doc: last record of the seen-stream list: stream_seen_add links the new record through it and then points it at the new record; stream_seen_clear zeroes it with streamSeenHead. Nothing else reads it

thingNodeQueue.doc: int[150] of detail-record indices, one per THNG chunk: project_chunk_exec passes the chunk's +8 short id through project_mangle_id and project_detail_find and appends the result, system_error when the id has no detail, silently dropping it past 0x96. sim_load_by_name fills it with -1 and zeroes both counters once per mission load, so it is shared across every gamepiece stream. CONSUMER: thing_node_queue_pop, called exactly twice by mech_std_create and mech_alt_create, storing MechLoadout.torsoNode then weaponAimNode. Pairing holds because the GP chunk that creates the gamepiece follows its own two THNGs; a GP with none pops nothing, since the two counters are then equal, and both nodes stay null

missionTables.doc: sixteen pointers, each to a table the project file supplied through config_table_load. An entry is a copy of the chunk itself: an 8-byte header and then records of 0x97 bytes, with a name at +0x70 that mission_mark_by_name (formerly mech_config_sub_04d550) searches on. THE RECORDS ARE MISSION OBJECTIVES - see missionRecordState for the consumer that settles it. STATIC RECORD LAYOUT, from objective_table_install and checked against the MTBL chunks in MW2.PRJ: the chunk has an 8-byte chunk header, then +8 the table slot, +0xc a dword, and two 11-byte resource names at +0x12 and +0x1d. Those end in S and F in the data ('gene001S', 'gene001F') and each is resolved with resource_id_by_name (formerly geom_table_tabl_handler)(0xb, name). They are the MISSION SUCCESS and FAILURE announcements: mission_result_text plays the +0x12 one beside 'Mission successful' when the table's result byte (objectiveTableResult) is 2, and the +0x1d one beside 'Mission failed' when it is 3. Records of 0x97 bytes start at +0x26; the first record's type must be 0x10 or it is system_error. Within a record: +0x00 type dword (0x10, 2, 4, 0x200 seen); +0x04 'V' or 'H', and 'V' makes the objective listed; +0x06 how the prerequisites combine - 0 means any one is enough, anything else means all are needed (objective_is_active); +0x0a eight PREREQUISITE entries of {letter, record, table}, naming another objective. The letter maps C -> 1, completed, i.e. Successful or Failed; S -> 2, Successful; F -> 3, Failed; anything else (including the 'I' the data uses) -> 0, which ENDS the list (objective_prereq_met). An objective with no prerequisites is never active unless its type is 0x10. The data's first 'C' entry, (C, 0, 1), reads 'once objective 0 of table 1 is completed'; +0x2a a dword; +0x2e the category byte; +0x2f 'M' or 'O', copied into the runtime flag at +0x5d - an objective of type 0x20 cannot succeed until every other 'M' objective is Successful, which is what M is established to mean; 'O' objectives are not waited for, and nothing else about the letters is established; +0x30 and +0x31 bytes; +0x34 and +0x3f the objective's own SUCCESS and FAILURE announcements, another S/F pair of names. For the player's group, mission_result_format plays the +0x34 one with '%s successful' when the objective reaches state 5, and the +0x3f one with '%s failed' at state 6. The %s is the objective text, posted only if the objective is listed, and each objective is announced once; +0x4a the objective's identifier ('amy_st01', 'amy_ens1'), which is what mission_mark_by_name searches; +0x53 and +0x55 ushorts; +0x57 the objective TEXT, e.g. 'Drop Site: Omega' and 'Destroy First Mech Star'. The count of sixteen has two independent sources - config_tables_free loops to 0x10, and configTableCounts starts 0x40 bytes later, which is sixteen pointers exactly. RESOLVED, and the answer renames these: the only caller of the loader is the handler for the MTBL chunk, which the project vocabulary calls mission_table, so these are MISSION records and the name at +0x70 is a mission name. Two earlier passes left the contents unestablished and called everything config*; that was right on the evidence then - the tables are filled by slot index, so nothing inside them says what they are - and the tag dispatch is what settled it. CORRECTION: this said 'Individual record FIELDS are still unread'. They are no longer: this global is typed MissionTableChunk *[16], and every record field is laid out, each with its reader, in MissionObjectiveRecord (MissionTableChunk.records) and printed by tools/dump_objectives.py. STATIC +0x30 and +0x31, from the installer disassembly (0x4d2e0, 0x4d2ff): +0x30 is copied to runtime +0x61, the per-target member quota group_assign_objective_task fills (0 = every member). +0x31 is copied to runtime +0x65, Objective.restraint, which group_apply_objective and group_assign_objective_task turn into aiFlags 0x42 for 1 and 0x41 for 2 (else 0x40): 1 keeps tasked mechs from being dispatched after threats, 2 also stops them retaliating (this said 'what those bits do is not established' until their readers were traced). Both are printed by dump_objectives as quota and restraint

configTableCounts.doc: how many records each configTables entry holds, computed as (chunk size - 8) / 0x97 when the table is installed

polyCodeRemapTable.doc: pointer to a table of dwords poly_resolve_code would look a polygon code up in: for a code with bit 0x8000 it clears the bit and, when this is non-null and the result is <= polyCodeRemapLimit, replaces the code with table[code]. NEVER SET: 0 in the image (BSS), and a sweep of the whole image for the address as a 32-bit value finds only poly_resolve_code's two reads (0x4fe4c, 0x4fe74) - no store, no lea, no pointer in data; the nearest lower global another routine addresses, scenarioTableCount at 0x1538d8, is only ever read and written directly. And no polygon in MW2.PRJ uses the path: none of the 85594 WTBO polygon codes has bit 0x8000. FOR A PORT: nothing to implement - at most, clear bit 0x8000

wtboLodMode.doc: set by poly_load_wtbo_record for WTBO flag 0x1000 when 0x2000 is clear, cleared with wtboPartMode. While set the digits after the '_' in a record's name become its key, and a record after the first is added to the current object as another mesh (object_add_mesh) instead of building an object - the level-of-detail meshes object_draw_lod_mesh switches between by that key. All four references are in poly_load_wtbo_record

wtboPartMode.doc: set by poly_load_wtbo_record when a WTBO record's flags have 0x2000, and cleared only when a new object starts (*objOut == 0), so it holds for the rest of the block. While set, EVERY record becomes its own object (object_create) on its own scene node, and the record's LAST VERTEX IS NOT GEOMETRY: only count - 1 vertices go to mesh_add_vertex, and the last one's raw x, y, z (before polyVertexScale and polyVertexOffset) goes to scene_node_set_origin - it is the part's pivot. CHECKED against MW2.PRJ: in all 1195 records with flag 0x2000 no polygon indexes the last vertex, while in all 4599 other records one does. Every part after the first (nodeCount != 0) is also object_link'ed, given objectClass wtboPartClass (4) and type 0x50. All five code references are in poly_load_wtbo_record; the address's other two byte matches, inside clib_dos4g_sub_081514, are not instruction operands

polyOwnerActive.doc: non-zero while a mesh is being built for a specific mech or gamething - mech_apply_detail_level and the world-record mesh loader set it around poly_load_wtbo_block and clear it after. poly_resolve_code only applies the owner's affiliation while it is set

polyOwnerKind.doc: 0x100 when the owner is a mech (mech_apply_detail_level), 0x200 when it is a gamething (the world-record loader); poly_resolve_code picks MechGroup.affiliation or GameThing.affiliation on it

polyOwnerIndex.doc: the mech index or gamething index polyOwnerKind refers to

savedLight.doc: effect_spawn's save area for the mission's light while an effect is lighting the scene: lightPos x, y, z at +0, +4, +8, lightDirectional at +0xc, ambientLight at +0x10, the 0x9705c flag at +0x14; sim_slots_update restores all six

nukeBlastX.doc: x of the active nuke blast's centre; nuke_detonate sets it from the detonating mech's posX. nukeBlastY and nukeBlastZ follow at +4 and +8

nukeBlastY.doc: y of the nuke blast centre - see nukeBlastX

nukeBlastZ.doc: z of the nuke blast centre - see nukeBlastX

nukeBlastRadius.doc: the nuke blast's current radius in cm: 0 at detonation, + 200 * tickDelta per tick in nuke_blast_update, capped at nukeBlastMaxRadius

nukeBlastMaxRadius.doc: the cap on nukeBlastRadius: 400000 cm (4 km) by default, or 100 x the radius of a live type-0x16 simSlot's object, set by nuke_detonate

missileCamPose.doc: the missile camera's pose, seven dwords: +0 x, +4 y, +8 z, +0xc yaw, +0x10 pitch, +0x14 roll, +0x18 valid. While a projectile's missileCam is set, projectile_update writes its position, yaw = fixed_atan2(velX, velZ), pitch and roll 0, and valid 1. So the camera rides the missile looking along its horizontal heading, level. sim_tables_reset zeroes all seven. The camera update copies x..roll into viewerPosition when valid is set

netplayWeaponFiredLocal.doc: int[10], the OUTGOING half of netplayWeaponFired: entry i is set to 1 when this machine's mech fires the weapon whose MechWeapon.originalIndex is i (three fire paths store it, in cockpit.c, mech_weapons_tick (whose second half was once split off as mech_weapons_tick_tail) and unsorted.c). netplay_build_state (formerly netplay_sub_044b70), building the outgoing state packet, ORs bit 5+i of the packet word at +3 for each set entry and clears it. That is the exact word and bit range the receive side decodes into netplayWeaponFired. mech_weapons_cancel_bursts zeroes it

netplayWeaponFired.doc: int[10], one per weapon slot: 1 means a remote mech's state packet said that weapon fired. The netplay receive path (in netplay_apply_state (formerly netplay_opponent_killed)) sets entry i when bit 5+i of the packet word at +3 is set, and netplay_weapons_start_burst clears each set entry as it starts that weapon's burst. Those are its only two references

crosshairObject.doc: the world object the player's fire ray last hit that was a mech or a gamething, set only by mech_update_aim_range and only for the player's mech. player_target_reticle (formerly ai_autopilot_update) turns it into a target: object type bit 0x100 validates the object's +0x14 id as a mech and makes the handle id | 0x200, bit 0x200 as a gamething with id | 0x400. When it is 0 that function does nothing. It is never cleared by the aim code, so it names the last such object aimed at, not necessarily the one under the crosshair now
